<i class="fa icon-warning" title="Warning"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
Changing the membership type affects the lifecycle of the member’s account. When changing from <strong>Unmanaged</strong> to <strong>Managed</strong>,
the member’s account becomes bound to the organization — removing the member from the organization or deleting the organization will also remove the account from the realm.
Conversely, changing from <strong>Managed</strong> to <strong>Unmanaged</strong> means the account will persist in the realm even if the member is removed from the organization, but the user may lack local credentials if originally federated via an identity provider.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="adding-an-existing-realm-user-as-a-member"><a class="anchor" href="#adding-an-existing-realm-user-as-a-member"></a>Adding an existing realm user as a member</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>An existing realm user can join an organization by selecting that user from a list and adding the user to the organization.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add member</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add realm user</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select one or more users and click <strong>Add</strong> to add them to the organization.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<div class="title">Adding a realm user</div>
<p><span class="image"><img src="./images/organizations-add-realm-user.png" alt="Adding a realm user"></span></p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Once a user is a member of the organization, that user is able to authenticate to the realm just like a regular user and using
any credential supported by the realm.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="inviting-users"><a class="anchor" href="#inviting-users"></a>Inviting users</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>An administrator can email users to join an organization.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add member</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Invite member</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Provide an email address</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Send</strong></p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<div class="title">Inviting members</div>
<p><span class="image"><img src="./images/organizations-invite-member.png" alt="Inviting members"></span></p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Optionally, you can also provide a value for the <strong>First name</strong> and <strong>Last name</strong> fields for a more personalized email
message using a greeting message with the first and last names of the person receiving the email.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>An invitation is basically an email sent with a link that the person should click to perform the necessary steps to join
an organization. These steps depend on whether the person already has an account in the realm or if a new account should
be created before joining the organization.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If the email maps to an existing user in a realm, the steps the user will follow are basically about confirming the
intention to join the organization.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>On the other hand, if no user is associated with the given email address, the steps
will involve creating a new account through the realm’s self-registration flow. In this case, the user is forced
to provide the same email address used to send the invitation.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="managing-invitations"><a class="anchor" href="#managing-invitations"></a>Managing invitations</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Keycloak provides comprehensive invitation management capabilities that allow administrators to track, manage, and control
organization invitations throughout their lifecycle.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="viewing-invitations"><a class="anchor" href="#viewing-invitations"></a>Viewing invitations</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To view and manage all invitations for an organization:</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Select the organization you want to manage.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <strong>Invitations</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The invitations list displays all sent invitations with the following information:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Email</strong> - The email address of the invited user</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Status</strong> - Current status of the invitation (Pending, Expired)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Created</strong> - When the invitation was sent</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Expires</strong> - When the invitation will expire (if applicable)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can filter invitations by status to easily find pending or expired invitations.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="managing-invitation-lifecycle"><a class="anchor" href="#managing-invitation-lifecycle"></a>Managing invitation lifecycle</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Administrators can perform various actions on invitations:</p>
</div>
<div class="sect5">
<h6 id="resending-invitations"><a class="anchor" href="#resending-invitations"></a>Resending invitations</h6>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To resend a pending invitation:</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>From the invitations list, locate the invitation you want to resend.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the action menu next to the invitation.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select <strong>Resend</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A new invitation email will be sent to the recipient with a fresh expiration time.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect5">
<h6 id="deleting-invitations"><a class="anchor" href="#deleting-invitations"></a>Deleting invitations</h6>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To permanently delete an invitation record:</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>From the invitations list, locate the invitation you want to delete.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the action menu next to the invitation.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select <strong>Delete</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Confirm the deletion.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This permanently removes the invitation from the system. This action cannot be undone.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="invitation-states-and-lifecycle"><a class="anchor" href="#invitation-states-and-lifecycle"></a>Invitation states and lifecycle</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Invitations go through several states during their lifecycle:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Pending</strong> - The invitation has been sent and is waiting for the recipient to accept</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Expired</strong> - The invitation has passed its expiration time</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
When a user successfully accepts an invitation, the invitation is automatically deleted from the system.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="api-access"><a class="anchor" href="#api-access"></a>API access</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Organization invitations can also be managed programmatically through the Admin REST API:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>GET /admin/realms/{realm}/orgs/{orgId}/invitations</code> - List all invitations</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>GET /admin/realms/{realm}/orgs/{orgId}/invitations/{invitationId}</code> - Get specific invitation</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>POST /admin/realms/{realm}/orgs/{orgId}/invitations/{invitationId}/resend</code> - Resend invitation</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/orgs/{orgId}/invitations/{invitationId}</code> - Delete invitation</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For detailed API documentation, refer to the Keycloak Admin REST API documentation.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_onboard_member_identity_provider_"><a class="anchor" href="#_onboard_member_identity_provider_"></a>Onboarding members using an Identity Provider</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>An organization might have its own identity provider as the single source of truth for their identities. In this case,
users federated from the identity provider can be automatically added as members of the organization, provided the identity provider link has auto membership enabled and the user’s email domain passes the domain gate.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When users join an organization through an identity provider, the membership type assigned to them
depends on the per-association configuration of the identity provider link. By default, new links use the unmanaged membership type,
but this can be changed to managed when linking the identity provider to the organization. Users go through the broker login flows
configured in the realm and join the organization once they successfully authenticate, subject to the per-association and domain gate checks described in <a href="#authenticating-members_server_administration_guide">Authenticating members</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Onboarding new members through an identity provider can be done by either automatically redirecting the user to an organization’s
identity provider or by selecting the identity provider when at the login page.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In both cases, once the user provides the email, Keycloak will try to match an organization based on the email domain. In case
the email domain matches the organization, and a domain is configured to route to an identity provider with <strong>Auto redirect</strong>
enabled, the user is automatically redirected to the identity provider. Once the user authenticates at the identity provider
and completes the first broker login flow, the user is automatically added as an organization member.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>On the other hand, if <strong>Auto redirect</strong> is not enabled on the domain, but the identity provider is configured not to
<strong>Hide on login page</strong>, the user can select the identity provider and then be redirected to the identity provider to continue
the onboarding process.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For more details, see <a href="#_managing_identity_provider_">Managing Identity Providers</a>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="removing-a-member"><a class="anchor" href="#removing-a-member"></a>Removing a member</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can remove a member from an organization.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>From the action menu next to the member you want to remove, click <strong>Remove</strong>.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When removing a member from an organization, remember that the user may or may not be removed from a realm depending on if
that user is managed or unmanaged member, respectively.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For more details, see <a href="#_managed_unmanaged_members_">Managed and unmanaged members</a>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="viewing-organization-group-memberships"><a class="anchor" href="#viewing-organization-group-memberships"></a>Viewing organization group memberships</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can view which organization groups a member belongs to directly from the member’s context menu.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>To view group memberships from the <strong>Members</strong> tab:</p>
<div class="olist loweralpha">
<ol class="loweralpha" type="a">
<li>
<p>Navigate to your organization.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <strong>Members</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Locate the member.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the kebab menu (⋮) next to the member.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select <strong>Show organization group memberships</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>To view group memberships from a specific group:</p>
<div class="olist loweralpha">
<ol class="loweralpha" type="a">
<li>
<p>Navigate to your organization.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <strong>Groups</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select the group.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <strong>Members</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Locate the member.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the kebab menu (⋮) next to the member.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select <strong>Show memberships</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>To view group memberships from the user’s detail page:</p>
<div class="olist loweralpha">
<ol class="loweralpha" type="a">
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Users</strong> in the menu.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select the user.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <strong>Organizations</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Locate the organization.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the kebab menu (⋮) next to the organization.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select <strong>Show organization group memberships</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This displays all groups from the specific organization the member is currently assigned to.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="support-for-federated-members"><a class="anchor" href="#support-for-federated-members"></a>Support for federated members</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Users coming from federated providers can also be added as members of an organization. The only exceptions are the users from LDAP providers with <strong>import mode disabled</strong>. Organization members are added to an internal group that is not synchronized with external providers, so even if the LDAP provider has a group mapper with mode LDAP_ONLY it won’t be possible for the non-imported users to be added as members of an organization because that membership won’t be synced with the LDAP server.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In other words, LDAP users that are not imported can’t join an organization because the membership is not stored in the local DB nor in the LDAP server. So if you want to have LDAP users joining organizations, ensure that the import mode of the LDAP provider is enabled.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_managing_groups_"><a class="anchor" href="#_managing_groups_"></a>Managing groups</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/organizations/managing-groups.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/organizations/managing-groups.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/organizations/managing-groups.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph _abstract">
<p>Organization groups let you organize members into logical teams, departments, or any hierarchical structure that makes sense for your organization. Think of them as folders for your users—simple, flexible, and powerful.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Unlike realm groups that are shared across your entire realm, organization groups belong exclusively to one organization. This means <code>orgA</code> and <code>orgB</code> can each have a <code>/Engineering/Backend</code> group without any conflict—each is a completely separate group with its own unique identifier.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="creating-groups"><a class="anchor" href="#creating-groups"></a>Creating groups</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Navigate to your organization and click the <strong>Groups</strong> tab.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<div class="title">Managing organization groups</div>
<p><span class="image"><img src="./images/organizations-manage-groups.png" alt="Managing organization groups"></span></p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Create group</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Provide a <strong>Name</strong> for the group.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Create</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Optionally, before creating the group, navigate to <strong>Parent group</strong> to create nested structures.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Your group is ready. You can now add members, nest more groups under it, or set attributes.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="building-hierarchies"><a class="anchor" href="#building-hierarchies"></a>Building hierarchies</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Groups can be nested to create organizational structures that mirror your real-world teams:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code>/Engineering
  /Engineering/Backend
  /Engineering/Frontend
/Sales
  /Sales/APAC
  /Sales/EMEA
  /Sales/LATAM
  /Sales/NA</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Create a child group by selecting its parent before creation, or move groups, by clicking <strong>Move to</strong> in the UI to reorganize them.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="adding-members-to-groups"><a class="anchor" href="#adding-members-to-groups"></a>Adding members to groups</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Members join groups the same way they join realm groups.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Select the group.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <strong>Members</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add member</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select one or more organization members.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
To automatically assign members to these groups when they authenticate via an Identity Provider, see <a href="#_managing_identity_provider_">Mapping federated users to organization groups</a>.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock tip">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-tip" title="Tip"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
To view which organization groups a specific member belongs to, use the kebab menu (⋮) next to the member and select <strong>Show group memberships</strong>. For details, see <a href="#viewing-organization-group-memberships">Viewing organization group memberships</a>.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="understanding-group-paths"><a class="anchor" href="#understanding-group-paths"></a>Understanding group paths</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Every group has a path that describes its location in the hierarchy. Paths are <strong>relative to the organization</strong>, not the realm.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For example:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Organization A has <code>/Engineering/Backend</code></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Organization B has <code>/Engineering/Backend</code></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>The realm also has <code>/Engineering/Backend</code></p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>These are three completely separate groups. When you reference <code>/Engineering/Backend</code> in the context of Organization A, you’re talking about Organization A’s group—period.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This isolation is intentional. Your organizations remain independent, and you can structure each one however you need without worrying about naming conflicts.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="mapping-groups-to-tokens"><a class="anchor" href="#mapping-groups-to-tokens"></a>Mapping groups to tokens</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Organization group membership can appear in tokens for both OIDC and SAML protocols. The setup differs between protocols.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="oidc-organization-groups-in-tokens"><a class="anchor" href="#oidc-organization-groups-in-tokens"></a>OIDC: Organization groups in tokens</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Organization groups are added to the <code>organization</code> claim alongside other organization data. To include groups in OIDC tokens, you must configure the mapper AND request the appropriate scope.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock important">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-important" title="Important"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
The <strong>Organization Group Membership</strong> mapper alone is NOT sufficient. It only works when combined with the <strong>Organization Membership</strong> mapper in the same scope.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="sect5">
<h6 id="option-1-add-mapper-to-built-in-organization-scope-recommended"><a class="anchor" href="#option-1-add-mapper-to-built-in-organization-scope-recommended"></a>Option 1: Add mapper to built-in organization scope (Recommended)</h6>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The built-in <code>organization</code> scope already has the Organization Membership mapper. Simply add the group mapper to it.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Client scopes</strong> in the menu.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select the <strong>organization</strong> scope.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <strong>Mappers</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add mapper</strong> → <strong>By configuration</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select <strong>Organization Group Membership</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Configure the mapper:</p>
<div class="dlist">
<dl>
<dt class="hdlist1">Add to ID token</dt>
<dd>
<p>Include groups in ID tokens.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1">Add to access token</dt>
<dd>
<p>Include groups in access tokens.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1">Add to lightweight access token</dt>
<dd>
<p>Include groups in lightweight access tokens.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1">Add to userinfo</dt>
<dd>
<p>Include groups in the UserInfo endpoint response.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1">Add to introspection</dt>
<dd>
<p>Include groups in the Introspection endpoint response.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1">Add group role mappings</dt>
<dd>
<p>When enabled, realm and client roles assigned to the user’s organization groups are included in the token for each organization. See <a href="#oidc-token-with-roles">Token structure with roles</a> for the output format.</p>
</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The <code>organization</code> scope is added as an optional scope to all clients by default. Applications request it using <code>scope=organization</code> (or <code>scope=organization:alias</code> for a specific organization, or multiple specific organizations like <code>scope=organization:org-a organization:org-b</code>).</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect5">
<h6 id="option-2-create-custom-scope-with-both-mappers"><a class="anchor" href="#option-2-create-custom-scope-with-both-mappers"></a>Option 2: Create custom scope with both mappers</h6>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If you need a dedicated scope for organization data, create one with BOTH required mappers.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Client scopes</strong> in the menu.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Create client scope</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Provide a <strong>Name</strong> (for example, <code>my-org-scope</code>).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Set <strong>Protocol</strong> to <strong>OpenID Connect</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <strong>Mappers</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Add BOTH mappers:</p>
<div class="olist loweralpha">
<ol class="loweralpha" type="a">
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Configure a new mapper</strong> → <strong>Organization Membership</strong></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Configure and save</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add mapper</strong> → <strong>By configuration</strong> → <strong>Organization Group Membership</strong></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Configure and save</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Go to your client.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Client scopes</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add client scope</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select your custom scope.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Choose <strong>Default</strong> or <strong>Optional</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Applications request it using <code>scope=my-org-scope</code>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect5">
<h6 id="token-structure"><a class="anchor" href="#token-structure"></a>Token structure</h6>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When a user from Organization A’s <code>/Engineering/Backend</code> group authenticates and requests the organization scope, the token includes:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="json">{
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">organization</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: {
    <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">orgA</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: {
      <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">id</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">f8d3c4e1-...</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>,
      <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">groups</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: [ <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">/Engineering/Backend</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span> ]
    }
  }
}</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Notice:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Groups appear within the organization claim, not as a separate top-level claim</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Group paths are relative to the organization</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Make sure you have a single <code>organization-membership</code> mapper so that groups are included in the same claim as the organization data</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Multiple organizations can be included if the user is a member of multiple organizations and uses <code>scope=organization:*</code> or multiple specific scopes like <code>scope=organization:org-a organization:org-b</code></p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect5">
<h6 id="oidc-token-with-roles"><a class="anchor" href="#oidc-token-with-roles"></a>Token structure with roles</h6>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When <strong>Add group role mappings</strong> is enabled on the mapper, realm and client roles assigned to the user’s organization groups are included under <code>realm_access</code> and <code>resource_access</code> keys, following the same structure as standard Keycloak token role claims:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="json">{
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">organization</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: {
    <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">orgA</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: {
      <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">id</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">f8d3c4e1-...</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>,
      <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">groups</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: [ <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">/Engineering/Backend</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span> ],
      <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">realm_access</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: {
        <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">roles</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: [ <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">org-admin</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>, <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">viewer</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span> ]
      },
      <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">resource_access</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: {
        <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">my-client</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: {
          <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">roles</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: [ <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">client-editor</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span> ]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Composite roles are automatically expanded—if a group has a composite role, all its child roles are included.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
These roles are specific to the organization context and appear inside the <code>organization</code> claim. Standard <code>realm_access</code> and <code>resource_access</code> claims already include roles from all groups (including organization groups) regardless of this mapper setting.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="saml-organization-groups-in-assertions"><a class="anchor" href="#saml-organization-groups-in-assertions"></a>SAML: Organization groups in assertions</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>SAML automatically includes groups for all organizations the user is a member of. Like OIDC, the group mapper requires the organization membership mapper to be present in the same scope.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect5">
<h6 id="option-1-add-mapper-to-built-in-saml_organization-scope-recommended"><a class="anchor" href="#option-1-add-mapper-to-built-in-saml_organization-scope-recommended"></a>Option 1: Add mapper to built-in saml_organization scope (Recommended)</h6>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The built-in <code>saml_organization</code> scope already has the Organization Membership mapper and is added as a default scope to all SAML clients. Simply add the group mapper to it.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Client scopes</strong> in the menu.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select the <strong>saml_organization</strong> scope.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <strong>Mappers</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add mapper</strong> → <strong>By configuration</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select <strong>Organization Group Membership</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The mapper has one optional configuration:</p>
</div>
<div class="dlist">
<dl>
<dt class="hdlist1">Add group role mappings</dt>
<dd>
<p>When enabled, realm and client roles assigned to the user’s organization groups are included as additional SAML attributes. See <a href="#saml-assertion-with-roles">SAML assertion structure with roles</a> for the output format.</p>
</dd>
</dl>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Groups are automatically included for all SAML clients.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect5">
<h6 id="option-2-create-custom-saml-scope-with-both-mappers"><a class="anchor" href="#option-2-create-custom-saml-scope-with-both-mappers"></a>Option 2: Create custom SAML scope with both mappers</h6>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If you need a dedicated scope, create one with both the membership and group mappers.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Client scopes</strong> in the menu.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Create client scope</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Provide a <strong>Name</strong> (for example, <code>my-saml-org-scope</code>).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Set <strong>Protocol</strong> to <strong>SAML</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <strong>Mappers</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Add BOTH mappers:</p>
<div class="olist loweralpha">
<ol class="loweralpha" type="a">
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Configure a new mapper</strong> → <strong>Organization Membership</strong></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add mapper</strong> → <strong>By configuration</strong> → <strong>Organization Group Membership</strong></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong></p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Go to your SAML client.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Client scopes</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add client scope</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select your custom scope.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Choose <strong>Default</strong> or <strong>Optional</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect5">
<h6 id="saml-assertion-structure"><a class="anchor" href="#saml-assertion-structure"></a>SAML assertion structure</h6>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When a user from Organization A’s <code>/Engineering/Backend</code> group authenticates, the assertion includes attributes for each organization they belong to:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="xml"><span class="tag"><Attribute</span> <span class="attribute-name">Name</span>=<span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">organization.orgA.groups</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span><span class="tag">></span>
  <span class="tag"><AttributeValue></span>/Engineering/Backend<span class="tag"></AttributeValue></span>
<span class="tag"></Attribute></span></code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Each organization gets its own attribute named <code>organization.{alias}.groups</code> with group paths as values, where <code>alias</code> is the organization alias.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect5">
<h6 id="saml-assertion-with-roles"><a class="anchor" href="#saml-assertion-with-roles"></a>SAML assertion structure with roles</h6>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When <strong>Add group role mappings</strong> is enabled on the mapper, realm and client roles assigned to the user’s organization groups are included as additional attributes:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="xml"><span class="tag"><Attribute</span> <span class="attribute-name">Name</span>=<span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">organization.orgA.groups</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span><span class="tag">></span>
  <span class="tag"><AttributeValue></span>/Engineering/Backend<span class="tag"></AttributeValue></span>
<span class="tag"></Attribute></span>
<span class="tag"><Attribute</span> <span class="attribute-name">Name</span>=<span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">organization.orgA.realm_access.roles</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span><span class="tag">></span>
  <span class="tag"><AttributeValue></span>org-admin<span class="tag"></AttributeValue></span>
  <span class="tag"><AttributeValue></span>viewer<span class="tag"></AttributeValue></span>
<span class="tag"></Attribute></span>
<span class="tag"><Attribute</span> <span class="attribute-name">Name</span>=<span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">organization.orgA.resource_access.my-client.roles</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span><span class="tag">></span>
  <span class="tag"><AttributeValue></span>client-editor<span class="tag"></AttributeValue></span>
<span class="tag"></Attribute></span></code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Composite roles are automatically expanded. Each role type uses a separate attribute:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>organization.{alias}.realm_access.roles</code> — realm roles from the user’s organization groups</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>organization.{alias}.resource_access.{clientId}.roles</code> — client roles, with one attribute per client</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
Unlike OIDC, SAML clients don’t need to request a scope at runtime. The <code>saml_organization</code> scope is added as a default scope, so groups are automatically included in assertions for all organizations the user is a member of.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="managing-group-attributes"><a class="anchor" href="#managing-group-attributes"></a>Managing group attributes</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Groups can carry attributes—key/value metadata stored at the group level.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Select a group.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <strong>Attributes</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Add attributes with keys and values.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Group attributes are stored separately from user attributes. To include group attributes in tokens, configure a <strong>User Attribute</strong> mapper with the <strong>Aggregate attributes</strong> option enabled. The mapper will then combine matching attributes from both the user and all their groups.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="assigning-roles-to-groups"><a class="anchor" href="#assigning-roles-to-groups"></a>Assigning roles to groups</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Organization groups support realm and client role mappings, just like realm groups. This lets you define role-based access that applies to all members of a group.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Select an organization group.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <strong>Role mapping</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Assign role</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select one or more realm or client roles.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Assign</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Roles assigned to organization groups are automatically included in <code>realm_access</code> and <code>resource_access</code> token claims for members of those groups—no additional mapper configuration is required.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To also include these roles within the <code>organization</code> claim (organized per organization), enable the <strong>Add group role mappings</strong> option on the <strong>Organization Group Membership</strong> mapper. See <a href="#oidc-token-with-roles">Token structure with roles</a> and <a href="#saml-assertion-with-roles">SAML assertion structure with roles</a> for details.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
Assigning roles to organization groups requires the <code>manage-organizations</code> realm admin role (or equivalent Fine-Grained Admin Permission on the organization) and the <code>map-role</code> permission on the specific role being assigned.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="important-distinctions"><a class="anchor" href="#important-distinctions"></a>Important distinctions</h4>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="organization-groups-vs-realm-groups"><a class="anchor" href="#organization-groups-vs-realm-groups"></a>Organization groups vs realm groups</h5>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33.3333%;">
<col style="width: 66.6667%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Feature</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Organization groups</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Scope</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Belong to a single organization</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Isolation</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Fully isolated—same paths can exist across organizations</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Role assignment</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Supported—realm and client roles can be assigned to organization groups via the Admin API and Admin Console</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Authorization policies</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Cannot be used in authorization policies—use realm groups instead</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Token mapping</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Appear in tokens when using organization context</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="authorization-policies-restriction"><a class="anchor" href="#authorization-policies-restriction"></a>Authorization policies restriction</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Organization groups <strong>cannot</strong> be used in Keycloak authorization policies. Only realm groups are supported for fine-grained authorization.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If you try to select an organization group when configuring a group-based policy, you’ll receive an error. This is intentional—authorization policies operate at the realm level, not the organization level.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="deleting-groups"><a class="anchor" href="#deleting-groups"></a>Deleting groups</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Deleting a group removes it and all its child groups. Members are <strong>not</strong> deleted—they simply lose their group membership.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Select the group.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Delete group</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Confirm the deletion.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_managing_identity_provider_"><a class="anchor" href="#_managing_identity_provider_"></a>Managing identity providers</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/organizations/managing-identity-providers.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/organizations/managing-identity-providers.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/organizations/managing-identity-providers.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph _abstract">
<p>An organization might have its own identity provider as the single source of truth for their identities. In this case,
you want to configure the organization to authenticate users using the organization’s identity provider, federate their
identities, and finally add them as a member of the organization.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>An organization can have one or more identity providers associated with it so that they can authenticate their users from
different sources and enforce different constraints on each of them.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A single identity provider can also be shared across multiple organizations. Each organization maintains its own independent
link to the identity provider, with per-association settings that control auto-membership and membership type. This enables
scenarios where a single corporate identity provider serves multiple business units, each with its own membership rules.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Before you can link an identity provider to an organization, you create an identity provider at the realm level from the <strong>Identity Providers</strong>
section in the menu. You can link any of the built-in social and identity providers available in the realm to an organization.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="linking-an-identity-provider-to-an-organization"><a class="anchor" href="#linking-an-identity-provider-to-an-organization"></a>Linking an identity provider to an organization</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>An identity provider can be linked to an organization from the <strong>Identity providers</strong> tab. If identity providers are already linked, you see a list of them with their per-association settings and options to edit or unlink.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<div class="title">Organization identity providers</div>
<p><span class="image"><img src="./images/organizations-identity-providers.png" alt="Organization identity providers"></span></p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Link identity provider</strong></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select an <strong>Identity provider</strong></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Configure the per-association settings</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong></p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<div class="title">Linking identity provider</div>
<p><span class="image"><img src="./images/organizations-link-identity-provider.png" alt="Linking identity provider"></span></p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When linking an identity provider to an organization, the following per-association settings are available:</p>
</div>
<div class="dlist">
<dl>
<dt class="hdlist1">Identity provider</dt>
<dd>
<p>The identity provider you want to link to the organization. A single identity provider can be linked to multiple organizations.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1">Auto membership</dt>
<dd>
<p>When enabled, users who authenticate through this identity provider are automatically added as members of the organization,
subject to the domain gate (see <a href="#authenticating-members_server_administration_guide">Authenticating members</a>). Enabled by default.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1">Membership type</dt>
<dd>
<p>The membership type assigned to users who are auto-added through this identity provider link.</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Unmanaged</strong> (default): the user’s account persists in the realm even if removed from the organization.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Managed</strong>: the user’s lifecycle is bound to the organization — removing the member or the organization also removes the account.</p>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The <strong>Managed</strong> option is only available when auto membership is enabled and no other organization has already claimed managed membership for this identity provider. At most one organization can have managed membership type for a given identity provider.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For more details on membership types, see <a href="#_managed_unmanaged_members_">Managed and unmanaged members</a>.</p>
</div>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</dd>
</dl>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
Setting auto membership to disabled while membership type is managed is not allowed. If you need invitation-only membership, set auto membership to disabled with the unmanaged membership type.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="identity-provider-display-settings"><a class="anchor" href="#identity-provider-display-settings"></a>Identity provider display settings</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Several settings control how an organization’s identity provider appears on the login page. These settings are configured on the identity provider itself (at the realm level) rather than on the per-organization link, because they apply globally regardless of which organization is involved.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To configure these settings, navigate to <strong>Identity Providers</strong> in the menu and select the provider.</p>
</div>
<div class="dlist">
<dl>
<dt class="hdlist1">Hide on login page</dt>
<dd>
<p>If this identity provider should be hidden on login pages when the user is authenticating in the scope of the organization. This setting is on the identity provider’s <strong>Settings</strong> tab.</p>
</dd>
</dl>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The remaining two settings are in the <strong>Organization settings</strong> section on the <strong>Settings</strong> tab. This section is visible only when the identity provider is linked to at least one organization.</p>
</div>
<div class="dlist">
<dl>
<dt class="hdlist1">Hide on login page when organization not resolved</dt>
<dd>
<p>If enabled, the identity provider will be hidden on the login page when the organization cannot be resolved based on the user’s email domain. Otherwise, the identity provider will be shown on the login page regardless of whether the organization is resolved or not. If <strong>Hide on login page</strong> is also enabled, the identity provider will always be hidden on the login page.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1">Show on login page for unlinked members</dt>
<dd>
<p>If enabled, organization members can see this identity provider on the login page even when they are already linked to another identity provider.</p>
</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="domain-routing"><a class="anchor" href="#domain-routing"></a>Domain routing</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Domain routing — which determines how users are redirected to an identity provider based on their email domain — is configured on the domain itself, not on the identity provider link. To configure which identity provider handles a specific domain and whether auto-redirect is enabled, see <a href="#managing-organization-domains_server_administration_guide">Managing organization domains</a>.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="understanding-per-association-configuration"><a class="anchor" href="#understanding-per-association-configuration"></a>Understanding per-association configuration</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Each link between an identity provider and an organization carries its own independent configuration. This means:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>The same identity provider can have different auto-membership and membership type settings for each organization it is linked to.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Changing the settings on one organization’s link does not affect other organizations linked to the same identity provider.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Unlinking an identity provider from one organization does not affect its links to other organizations.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The following validation rules apply:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>At most one organization per identity provider can have the <strong>Managed</strong> membership type. This prevents conflicting lifecycle ownership where multiple organizations could claim control over the same user’s account.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Auto membership disabled combined with managed membership type is not allowed. Managed membership requires auto-membership because the lifecycle binding depends on the automatic onboarding process.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="viewing-organizations-from-the-identity-provider-detail-page"><a class="anchor" href="#viewing-organizations-from-the-identity-provider-detail-page"></a>Viewing organizations from the identity provider detail page</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When an identity provider is linked to one or more organizations, its realm-level detail page displays an <strong>Organizations</strong> tab. This tab provides a reverse view — from the identity provider’s perspective — and contains two sub-tabs:</p>
</div>
<div class="dlist">
<dl>
<dt class="hdlist1">Organizations</dt>
<dd>
<p>Lists all organizations linked to this identity provider, showing the per-association auto membership and membership type settings for each. You can edit the per-association settings or unlink an organization directly from this view.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1">Domains</dt>
<dd>
<p>A read-only cross-reference of all organization domains that route to this identity provider. Each entry shows the domain name, the owning organization, and whether auto-redirect is enabled. To modify domain routing, navigate to the organization’s <strong>Domains</strong> tab.</p>
</dd>
</dl>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="mapping-federated-users-to-organization-groups"><a class="anchor" href="#mapping-federated-users-to-organization-groups"></a>Mapping federated users to organization groups</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When an identity provider is linked to an organization, you can configure mappers to automatically assign users authenticating through the IdP to organization groups based on claims or attributes from the external IdP.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect5">
<h6 id="using-the-hardcoded-group-mapper"><a class="anchor" href="#using-the-hardcoded-group-mapper"></a>Using the Hardcoded Group mapper</h6>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The Hardcoded Group mapper automatically adds all users authenticating through the IdP to a specific group.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Identity Providers</strong> in the menu.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select your identity provider linked to your organization.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <strong>Mappers</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add mapper</strong></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select <strong>Hardcoded Group</strong> mapper type.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Configure the mapper:</p>
<div class="dlist">
<dl>
<dt class="hdlist1">Name</dt>
<dd>
<p>A descriptive name for this mapper.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1">Sync Mode Override</dt>
<dd>
<p>How membership is managed (Import, Force, Inherit).</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1">Group</dt>
<dd>
<p>The group to assign users to. If the IdP is linked to one or more organizations, you can select realm groups or groups from a specific organization. The mapper stores the selected organization, so each mapper targets exactly one organization’s groups.</p>
</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock important">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-important" title="Important"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
If the identity provider is linked to multiple organizations, and you need to map users to groups in different organizations, create a separate mapper for each organization. If the IdP is unlinked from the mapper’s target organization, the organization group mapping becomes inactive and a warning is logged during authentication.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect5">
<h6 id="using-the-advanced-group-mapper"><a class="anchor" href="#using-the-advanced-group-mapper"></a>Using the Advanced Group mapper</h6>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The Advanced Group mapper assigns users to groups based on claim values from the external IdP.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Identity Providers</strong> in the menu.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select your identity provider linked to your organization.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <strong>Mappers</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add mapper</strong></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select <strong>Advanced Claim to Group</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Configure the mapper:</p>
<div class="dlist">
<dl>
<dt class="hdlist1">Name</dt>
<dd>
<p>A descriptive name for this mapper.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1">Sync Mode Override</dt>
<dd>
<p>How membership is managed (Import, Force, Inherit).</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1">Claims</dt>
<dd>
<p>Key-value pairs to match claims from the external IdP. Add claim names and their expected values. Users matching these claim values will be assigned to the specified group.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1">Regex Claim Values</dt>
<dd>
<p>When enabled, claim values are treated as regular expressions for pattern matching. When disabled, values must match exactly.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1">Group</dt>
<dd>
<p>The target group. If the IdP is linked to one or more organizations, you can select groups from a specific organization alongside realm groups.</p>
</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect5">
<h6 id="group-selection-behavior"><a class="anchor" href="#group-selection-behavior"></a>Group selection behavior</h6>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When configuring group mappers for an identity provider:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>IdP linked to one or more organizations:</strong> Both realm groups and groups from the selected organization are selectable. Each mapper targets one organization.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>IdP not linked to any organization:</strong> Only realm groups are selectable.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>IdP unlinked from the mapper’s target organization:</strong> Existing organization group mappings are preserved but no longer active.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect5">
<h6 id="runtime-validation"><a class="anchor" href="#runtime-validation"></a>Runtime validation</h6>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When a user authenticates through an identity provider:</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>The mapper checks if the IdP is still linked to an organization</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>If the IdP is unlinked, organization group mappings are skipped</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Only realm group mappings continue to work</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>A warning is logged to help administrators identify outdated mapper configurations</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Authentication continues successfully—no error is thrown to the user</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This ensures that unlinking an IdP from an organization doesn’t break authentication, but organization-specific mappings become inactive.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect5">
<h6 id="migration-considerations"><a class="anchor" href="#migration-considerations"></a>Migration considerations</h6>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If you unlink an identity provider from an organization:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Review all mappers on that IdP</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Update any mappers referencing organization groups</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Consider changing those mappings to realm groups if needed</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Alternatively, re-link the IdP to the organization to restore group mappings</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
Organization groups are isolated per organization. If you link an identity provider to a new organization, create new mappers targeting that organization’s groups. Existing mappers targeting the previous organization remain valid as long as that link is still active.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="editing-a-linked-identity-provider"><a class="anchor" href="#editing-a-linked-identity-provider"></a>Editing a linked identity provider</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can edit the per-association settings of a linked identity provider (such as auto membership and membership type) at any time.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>In the menu, click <strong>Organizations</strong> and go to the <strong>Identity providers</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Locate the <strong>identity provider</strong> in the list.</p>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can use the search option for this step.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the action button (three dots) at the end of the line.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Edit</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Make the necessary changes.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can also edit per-association settings from the identity provider’s realm-level detail page. Navigate to the <strong>Organizations</strong> tab and click <strong>Edit</strong> on the organization whose settings you want to change.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To edit the identity provider’s own settings (such as display options or organization settings), click the <strong>Provider details</strong> link in the identity providers list to navigate to the realm-level identity provider page.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="unlinking-an-identity-provider-from-an-organization"><a class="anchor" href="#unlinking-an-identity-provider-from-an-organization"></a>Unlinking an identity provider from an organization</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When an identity provider is unlinked from an organization, only the association between that organization and the identity provider is removed. The identity provider remains available as a realm-level provider and stays linked to any other organizations it is associated with.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To delete the unlinked provider entirely, use the <strong>Identity Providers</strong> section in the menu.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>In the menu, click <strong>Organizations</strong> and go to the <strong>Identity providers</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Locate the <strong>identity provider</strong> in the list.</p>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can use the search capabilities for this step.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the action button (three dots) at the end of the line.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Unlink provider</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can also unlink from the identity provider’s realm-level detail page by navigating to the <strong>Organizations</strong> tab and clicking <strong>Unlink</strong> on the organization.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="authenticating-members_server_administration_guide"><a class="anchor" href="#authenticating-members_server_administration_guide"></a>Authenticating members</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/organizations/authenticating-members.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/organizations/authenticating-members.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/organizations/authenticating-members.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph _abstract">
<p>When you enable organizations for a realm, user authentication is changed. If the user is recognized to be
authenticating in the context of an organization, the authentication flow changes on a per-organization basis.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When a realm is created, the authentication flows are automatically updated to enable specific steps to authenticate and onboard organization members. The authentication flows updated are:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>browser</strong></p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>first broker login</strong></p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The main change to the <strong>browser</strong> flow is that it defaults to an identity-first login so that users are identified before prompting for their credentials.
Concerning the first broker login flow, the main change is the ability to automatically add users as organization members once they authenticate through an identity provider associated with an organization and successfully complete the flow. Whether a user is actually added depends on the per-association configuration of the identity provider link — specifically the auto-membership and membership type settings (see <a href="#_managing_identity_provider_">Managing identity providers</a>) — and the domain gate, which checks that the user’s email domain is claimed by the organization.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The choice to use an identity-first login or not depends on the existence of an organization in a realm.
If no organizations exist, the user follows the usual steps to authenticate using the username and password,
or any other step configured in the browser flow. Otherwise, the user is asked first for a username or email to continue authenticating to a realm.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The identity-first login main goal is to identify the user:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Is the user an existing or a new user?</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Is the user a member of any organization within a realm?</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>If an organization member, is the user linked to any identity provider associated with the organization?</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Depending on the outcome when identifying the user, the authentication flow changes to either proceed with authentication
by asking for the user’s credentials or eventually redirect the user automatically to authenticate within the organization security
boundaries through an identity provider.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="understanding-the-identity-first-login"><a class="anchor" href="#understanding-the-identity-first-login"></a>Understanding the identity-first login</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In addition to identifying the user once the username is provided, the identity-first login is also responsible for:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Matching an email domain to an organization.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Deciding if the authentication flow should continue or not if an account already exists for the username provided</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Deciding how the user should be authenticated depending on how the domains and the identity providers are configured to an organization
and the set of credentials configured to the user account.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Seamlessly authenticating users through an identity provider when the user’s email domain matches a domain configured with identity provider routing and auto-redirect enabled.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The identity-first login provides the same capabilities that are provided by the usual login page with the username and
password fields. Users can still self-register by clicking the register link or choose any identity or social
broker that is not linked to an organization in that realm.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<div class="title">Identity-first login page</div>
<p><span class="image"><img src="./images/organizations-identity-first-login.png" alt="Identity-first login page"></span></p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In the case of a user that does not exist, if that user tries to authenticate using an email domain that matches an organization domain,
the identity-first login page appears again with a message that the username provided is not valid.
At this point, no need exists to ask the user for credentials.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<div class="title">Identity-first when user does not exist</div>
<p><span class="image"><img src="./images/organizations-identity-first-error.png" alt="Identity-first login error"></span></p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Several options exist to register the user allowing that user to authenticate to the realm and join an organization.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If the realm has the self-registration setting enabled, the user can click the <strong>Register</strong> link at the identity-first login page
and create an account at the realm.
After that, the administrator can send an invitation link to the user or manually add the user as a member of an organization.
For more details, see <a href="#_managing_members_">Managing members</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If the organization has an identity provider without a domain and the <strong>Hide on login page</strong> setting is <strong>OFF</strong>, users can also click
the identity provider link at the identity-first login page to automatically create an account and join an organization
once they authenticate through the identity provider.
For more details, see <a href="#_managing_identity_provider_">Managing identity providers</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In a similar situation to the previous section, the organization may have a domain configured to route to an identity provider
with auto-redirect enabled.
In this situation, the user is redirected to the identity provider if that user’s email matches the domain.
Once the flow completes, an account is created and the user joins the organization. In case the user has any first-factor credentials
configured (e.g.: password, passwordless, kerberos) to the account, the user is not automatically redirected to the identity provider but asked to authenticate using their
credentials.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="how-organization-membership-is-determined-during-broker-login"><a class="anchor" href="#how-organization-membership-is-determined-during-broker-login"></a>How organization membership is determined during broker login</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When a user authenticates through an identity provider that is linked to one or more organizations, the system determines
whether the user should be added as a member of an organization. This process involves several checks that run as part of
the first broker login flow.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="step-1-invitation-check"><a class="anchor" href="#step-1-invitation-check"></a>Step 1: Invitation check</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If the user is following an invitation link, the invitation determines which organization the user joins. The user is
added as an unmanaged member of the invited organization regardless of any identity provider link settings or domain
configuration. No further checks are performed.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="step-2-organization-resolution"><a class="anchor" href="#step-2-organization-resolution"></a>Step 2: Organization resolution</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The system determines which organization is the target of this login:</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p><strong>Auth session note</strong>: If the identity-first login resolved an organization from the user’s email domain, that organization is used.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Email domain match</strong>: The user’s email domain is matched against domains owned by organizations linked to this identity provider. Since each domain belongs to exactly one organization, this always identifies a single organization.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Single organization fallback</strong>: If only one organization is linked to this identity provider, it is selected automatically.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>No match</strong>: If no organization can be determined, no membership is added.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="step-3-resolved-organization-gate"><a class="anchor" href="#step-3-resolved-organization-gate"></a>Step 3: Resolved-organization gate</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If organization resolution identified a specific organization, only that organization is evaluated for membership.
This prevents membership in other organizations when the user’s login was initiated through a specific organization’s domain.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If no organization was resolved (for example, during an IdP-initiated login via <code>kc_idp_hint</code>), all organizations
linked to the identity provider are evaluated.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="step-4-per-association-and-domain-gate-checks"><a class="anchor" href="#step-4-per-association-and-domain-gate-checks"></a>Step 4: Per-association and domain gate checks</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For each candidate organization:</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p><strong>Auto membership disabled</strong>: If the identity provider link has auto membership set to disabled for this organization, the organization is skipped.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Auto membership enabled</strong>:</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>If the organization has no domains (domain-less organization), the domain gate is skipped and the user is added. This is useful for organizations that are domain-agnostic.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>If the organization has domains, the user’s email domain must match at least one domain owned by the organization. If there is no match, the organization is skipped.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="step-5-member-assignment"><a class="anchor" href="#step-5-member-assignment"></a>Step 5: Member assignment</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If all checks pass:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>If the user is already a member of the organization, they are not re-added and their membership type is not changed.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>If the user is new to the organization, they are added with the membership type configured on the identity provider link (managed or unmanaged).</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="login-flow-variations"><a class="anchor" href="#login-flow-variations"></a>Login flow variations</h5>
<div class="dlist">
<dl>
<dt class="hdlist1">SP-initiated login (email entered on login page)</dt>
<dd>
<p>The identity-first login resolves a specific organization from the user’s email domain. The resolved-organization gate
limits membership evaluation to that single organization. This is the most common flow.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1">IdP-initiated login (<code>kc_idp_hint</code>, no email entered)</dt>
<dd>
<p>No organization is pre-resolved. The post-broker membership step evaluates all organizations linked to the identity provider.
The domain gate still prevents cross-organization membership — users are only added to organizations whose domains match their email.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1">Invitation flow</dt>
<dd>
<p>The invitation bypasses the entire auto-membership algorithm. The user is added to the invited organization as an
unmanaged member, regardless of identity provider link settings or domain configuration.</p>
</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="configuring-existing-authentication-flows"><a class="anchor" href="#configuring-existing-authentication-flows"></a>Configuring existing authentication flows</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>As previously mentioned for new realms, authentication flows are automatically updated with the necessary steps
to support organizations and authenticate their members. For existing realms, in addition to enabling organizations to the
realm, you also need to manually update your existing (custom) authenticating flows.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Change the <strong>browser</strong> flow by following these steps:</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Duplicate the current flow bound to the <strong>Browser flow</strong> binding type to avoid breaking the flow you are currently using</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add sub-flow</strong> and give it a name such as <strong>My Organization</strong></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Move the newly added <strong>My Organization</strong> sub-flow to execute right after the <strong>Identity Provider Redirector</strong> execution step.
The main point here is that the sub-flow should happen before any other sub-flow or execution step that authenticates the
user using whatever credentials you support in your realm. Once added, change the <strong>Requirement</strong> to <strong>Alternative</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add sub-flow</strong> in the <strong>My Organization</strong> sub-flow and give it a name such as <strong>My Organization - Conditional</strong>. Once added, change the <strong>Requirement</strong> to <strong>Conditional</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add condition</strong> in the <strong>My Organization - Conditional</strong> sub-flow and select <strong>Condition - user configured</strong>. Once added, change the <strong>Requirement</strong> to <strong>Required</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add step</strong> in the <strong>My Organization - Conditional</strong> sub-flow and select the *Organization Identity-First Login</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>execution step. Once added, change the <strong>Requirement</strong> to <strong>Alternative</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Bind the authentication flow to the <strong>Browser</strong> binding type.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<div class="title">Organizations browser flow</div>
<p><span class="image"><img src="./images/organizations-browser-flow.png" alt="Organizations browser flow"></span></p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Once you enable the <a href="#_enabling_organization_">Organizations</a> setting to the realm and create
at least a single organization, you should be able to see the identity-first login page and start using organizations
in your realm.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Change the <strong>first broker login</strong> flow by following these steps:</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Duplicate the current flow bound to the <strong>First broker login flow</strong> bind type to avoid breaking the flow you are currently using</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add sub-flow</strong> and give it a name such as <code>Organization Member - Conditional</code>. Once added, change the <strong>Requirement</strong> to <strong>Conditional</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add condition</strong> in the <strong>Organization Member - Conditional</strong> sub-flow and select <strong>Condition - user configured</strong>. Once added, change the <strong>Requirement</strong> to <strong>Required</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Add step</strong> in the <strong>Organization Member - Conditional</strong> sub-flow and select the <strong>Organization Member Onboard</strong> execution step. Once added, change the <strong>Requirement</strong> to <strong>Required</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Bind the authentication flow to the <strong>First broker login</strong> binding type.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
