<div class="paragraph">
<div class="title">Organizations first broker flow</div>
<p><span class="image"><img src="./images/organizations-first-broker-flow.png" alt="Organizations first broker flow"></span></p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You should now be able to authenticate using any identity provider associated with an organization
and have the user joining the organization as a member as soon as they complete the first browser login flow.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="configuring-how-users-authenticate"><a class="anchor" href="#configuring-how-users-authenticate"></a>Configuring how users authenticate</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If the flow supports organizations, you can configure some of the steps to change how users authenticate to the realm.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For example, some use cases will require users to authenticate to a realm only if they are a member of any or a specific organization in the realm.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To enable this behavior, you need to enable the <code>Requires user membership</code> setting on the <code>Organization Identity-First Login</code> execution step by clicking on its settings.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If enabled, and after the user provides the username or email in the identity-first login page, the server will
try to resolve a organization where the user is a member by looking at any existing membership or based on the semantics of the <a href="#_mapping_organization_claims_">organization</a> scope,
if requested by the client. If not a member of an organization, an error page will be shown.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="common-organization-setup-recipes_server_administration_guide"><a class="anchor" href="#common-organization-setup-recipes_server_administration_guide"></a>Common setup recipes</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/organizations/common-setup-recipes.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/organizations/common-setup-recipes.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/organizations/common-setup-recipes.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This section provides step-by-step instructions for common organization configurations. Each recipe shows how to
achieve a specific outcome using identity provider links, domain routing, and auto-membership settings.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For the full details on the settings referenced in these recipes, see <a href="#_managing_identity_provider_">Managing identity providers</a>,
<a href="#managing-organization-domains_server_administration_guide">Managing organization domains</a>, and <a href="#authenticating-members_server_administration_guide">Authenticating members</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="single-identity-provider-with-automatic-managed-membership"><a class="anchor" href="#single-identity-provider-with-automatic-managed-membership"></a>Single identity provider with automatic managed membership</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><strong>Goal:</strong> Users from a known email domain authenticate through the organization’s identity provider and are automatically added as managed members.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><strong>Prerequisites:</strong> An identity provider created at the realm level.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Create an organization with a domain (for example, <code>acme.com</code>).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Go to the organization’s <strong>Identity providers</strong> tab and click <strong>Link identity provider</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select the identity provider, set <strong>Auto membership</strong> to <strong>ON</strong> and <strong>Membership type</strong> to <strong>Managed</strong>. Click <strong>Save</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Go to the organization’s <strong>Domains</strong> tab and click the domain (<code>acme.com</code>).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select the linked identity provider from the dropdown and enable <strong>Auto redirect</strong>. Click <strong>Save</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><strong>Result:</strong> When a user enters an email like <code>alice@acme.com</code> on the login page, they are automatically redirected to the identity provider. After authenticating, they are added to the organization as a managed member. If the organization or the membership is removed, the user’s account is also removed from the realm.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="multiple-domains-with-different-identity-providers"><a class="anchor" href="#multiple-domains-with-different-identity-providers"></a>Multiple domains with different identity providers</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><strong>Goal:</strong> A single organization authenticates users from different email domains through different identity providers, with different membership types.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><strong>Prerequisites:</strong> Two identity providers created at the realm level (for example, <code>idp-corporate</code> and <code>idp-partner</code>).</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Create an organization with two domains (for example, <code>acme.com</code> and <code>partner.com</code>).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Go to the organization’s <strong>Identity providers</strong> tab:</p>
<div class="olist loweralpha">
<ol class="loweralpha" type="a">
<li>
<p>Link <code>idp-corporate</code> with <strong>Auto membership</strong> ON and <strong>Membership type</strong> set to <strong>Managed</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Link <code>idp-partner</code> with <strong>Auto membership</strong> ON and <strong>Membership type</strong> set to <strong>Unmanaged</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Go to the organization’s <strong>Domains</strong> tab:</p>
<div class="olist loweralpha">
<ol class="loweralpha" type="a">
<li>
<p>Edit <code>acme.com</code>: select <code>idp-corporate</code>, enable <strong>Auto redirect</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Edit <code>partner.com</code>: select <code>idp-partner</code>, enable <strong>Auto redirect</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><strong>Result:</strong> Users with <code>@acme.com</code> emails are routed to <code>idp-corporate</code> and added as managed members. Users with <code>@partner.com</code> emails are routed to <code>idp-partner</code> and added as unmanaged members. The organization controls the membership type independently for each identity provider link.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="shared-identity-provider-across-multiple-organizations"><a class="anchor" href="#shared-identity-provider-across-multiple-organizations"></a>Shared identity provider across multiple organizations</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><strong>Goal:</strong> A single corporate identity provider (for example, a central EntraId instance) serves multiple organizations, with each organization only accepting users from its own email domain.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><strong>Prerequisites:</strong> One identity provider created at the realm level.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Create Org-A with domain <code>acme.com</code>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Create Org-B with domain <code>globex.com</code>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>In Org-A’s <strong>Identity providers</strong> tab: link the identity provider with <strong>Auto membership</strong> ON and the desired <strong>Membership type</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>In Org-A’s <strong>Domains</strong> tab: edit <code>acme.com</code>, select the identity provider, enable <strong>Auto redirect</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>In Org-B’s <strong>Identity providers</strong> tab: link the same identity provider with <strong>Auto membership</strong> ON and the desired <strong>Membership type</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>In Org-B’s <strong>Domains</strong> tab: edit <code>globex.com</code>, select the identity provider, enable <strong>Auto redirect</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><strong>Result:</strong> Both organizations share the same identity provider. The domain gate ensures that users with <code>@acme.com</code> are only added to Org-A, and users with <code>@globex.com</code> are only added to Org-B. A user whose email domain does not match either organization is not added to any organization.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
You can verify the shared configuration from the identity provider’s realm-level detail page. The <strong>Organizations</strong> tab shows both organizations with their per-association settings, and the <strong>Domains</strong> sub-tab shows all domains routing to this provider.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
At most one organization can set the membership type to <strong>Managed</strong> for a given identity provider. If Org-A uses <strong>Managed</strong>, Org-B must use <strong>Unmanaged</strong>.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="domain-less-organization-with-auto-membership"><a class="anchor" href="#domain-less-organization-with-auto-membership"></a>Domain-less organization with auto-membership</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><strong>Goal:</strong> An organization without domains automatically accepts any user who authenticates through a linked identity provider, regardless of their email domain.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><strong>Prerequisites:</strong> An identity provider created at the realm level.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Create an organization without any domains.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Go to the organization’s <strong>Identity providers</strong> tab and link the identity provider with <strong>Auto membership</strong> ON.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><strong>Result:</strong> Any user authenticating through this identity provider is added to the organization because the domain gate is skipped for organizations without domains.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock important">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-important" title="Important"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
When the identity provider is also linked to other organizations, the resolved-organization gate applies. If a user’s login was initiated through another organization’s domain (SP-initiated), the domain-less organization is skipped. The domain-less organization only receives members when it is the resolved organization (for example, via the <code>organization:alias</code> scope) or when no organization was resolved (for example, during IdP-initiated login via <code>kc_idp_hint</code>).
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="identity-provider-linked-without-auto-membership"><a class="anchor" href="#identity-provider-linked-without-auto-membership"></a>Identity provider linked without auto-membership</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><strong>Goal:</strong> Link an identity provider to an organization for login convenience without automatically adding users as members. Membership is managed through invitations or manual admin actions only.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><strong>Prerequisites:</strong> An identity provider created at the realm level.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Go to the organization’s <strong>Identity providers</strong> tab and link the identity provider.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Set <strong>Auto membership</strong> to <strong>OFF</strong>. The <strong>Membership type</strong> will be set to <strong>Unmanaged</strong> (managed is not available when auto membership is disabled).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><strong>Result:</strong> The identity provider is available on the login page (unless hidden), and users can authenticate through it. However, users are not automatically added as organization members. To add users to the organization, use invitations or add them manually as realm users.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="adding-members-through-invitations"><a class="anchor" href="#adding-members-through-invitations"></a>Adding members through invitations</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><strong>Goal:</strong> Invite a user to join an organization, regardless of identity provider or domain configuration.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><strong>Prerequisites:</strong> An organization exists.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Go to the organization’s <strong>Members</strong> tab and click <strong>Add member</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Invite member</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Provide the user’s email address and optionally a first and last name.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Send</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><strong>Result:</strong> The invited user receives an email with a link. When they click the link and authenticate (using any method, including an organization’s identity provider), they are added to the organization as an unmanaged member. The invitation flow bypasses all auto-membership and domain gate logic — the invitation determines the target organization directly.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
For more details on managing invitations, see <a href="#_managing_members_">Managing members</a>.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_mapping_organization_claims_"><a class="anchor" href="#_mapping_organization_claims_"></a>Mapping organization claims</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/organizations/mapping-organization-claims.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/organizations/mapping-organization-claims.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/organizations/mapping-organization-claims.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph _abstract">
<p>To map organization-specific claims into tokens, a client needs to request the <strong>organization</strong> scope when sending
authorization requests to the server. When authenticating in the context of an organization, clients can request the <code>organization</code> scope to map information
about the organizations where the user is a member.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>As a result, the token will contain a claim as follows:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="json"><span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">organization</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: {
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">testcorp</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: {
    <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">id</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">42c3e46f-2477-44d7-a85b-d3b43f6b31fa</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>,
    <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">attr1</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: [
      <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">value1</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>
    ]
  }
}</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The organization claim can be used by clients (for example, from ID Tokens) and resource servers (for example, from access tokens)
to authorize access to protected resources based on the organization where the user is a member.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The <code>organization</code> scope is a built-in optional client scope at the realm.  Therefore, this scope is added to any client created in the realm by default. It also defines the <code>Organization Membership</code> mapper that controls how the organization membership information is mapped to the tokens.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
By default, the organization id and attributes are not included in the organization claim. To include them, edit the mapper and enable the <strong>Add organization id</strong> and <strong>Add organization attributes</strong> options, respectively.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<div class="title">Including attributes in the organization claim</div>
<p><span class="image"><img src="./images/organizations-add-org-attrs-in-claim.png" alt="Including attributes in the organization claim"></span></p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The <code>organization</code> scope is requested using different formats:</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%;">
<col style="width: 50%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Format</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>organization</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Maps to a single organization if the user is a member of a single organization.
Otherwise, if a member of multiple organizations, the user will be prompted to select an organization when authenticating to the realm.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>organization:<alias></code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Maps to a specific organization with the given alias.
Multiple organizations can be requested by specifying multiple scopes, for example <code>organization:org-a organization:org-b</code>.
If any of the aliases does not match an existing organization or the user is not a member, the request will be rejected.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>organization:*</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Maps to all organizations the user is a member of.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
Mixing different scope formats (for example, <code>organization</code> with <code>organization:org-a</code>, or <code>organization:org-a</code> with <code>organization:*</code>) is not allowed and will result in an error.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For details on including organization groups in tokens, see <a href="#_managing_groups_">Managing groups</a>.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect1">
<h2 id="_managing_workflows"><a class="anchor" href="#_managing_workflows"></a>Managing workflows</h2>
<div class="sectionbody">
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/assembly-managing-workflows.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/assembly-managing-workflows.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/assembly-managing-workflows.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph _abstract">
<p>Keycloak Workflows is a powerful engine to automate and orchestrate realm administrative tasks, bringing key
capabilities of Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) to your identity and access management infrastructure.
By using workflows, you can implement policies and processes that govern the lifecycle of realm resources, such as users and clients,
helping you to improve security, meet compliance requirements, and reduce administrative costs.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>As a core component of IGA, identity lifecycle management is fully supported by workflows so that you can easily automate
onboarding and offboarding processes, and other recurring administrative tasks. For example, you can define workflows to:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Provision and de-provision realm resources, such as users, automatically based on specific events or conditions.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Automate Joiner-Mover-Leaver (JML) processes to ensure that users are granted the appropriate access rights based on their roles and responsibilities.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Enforce access reviews and certifications to ensure that users have the appropriate access rights.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Enforce Just-In-Time and Least Privilege access by automating role assignments and revocations.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Enforce strong authentication policies for realm users.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Prevent insider data breaches by automating the removal of inactive or obsolete users.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>By leveraging workflows, realm administrators can ensure that security policies are consistently enforced and based on
the least privilege principle, reduce the risk of human error, and free up valuable time to focus on other important administrative tasks.
This guide will walk you through the process of creating and managing workflows to automate your administrative tasks
and implement IGA best practices when managing realms.</p>
</div>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/workflows/intro.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/intro.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/intro.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_understanding_workflows_"><a class="anchor" href="#_understanding_workflows_"></a>Understanding workflows</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/workflows/understanding-workflow.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/understanding-workflow.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/understanding-workflow.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph _abstract">
<p>A workflow is an activity or process within Keycloak that executes a series of predefined steps on a
specific realm resource in response to specific events and based on the defined conditions.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In Keycloak, there are two main types of events:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>User Events</strong>: These events are initiated by users, such as login in or registering a new account.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Admin Events</strong>: These events are initiated by administrators through the Admin Console and API, such as creating or updating a user or any other realm resource.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Workflows are designed to respond to these events by automating tasks and processes that need to be performed and executed on the
realm resources associated with these events.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Once an event is fired, the workflow engine evaluates all defined workflows in the realm to determine if any should be
triggered based on the event type and the specified conditions. If the event matches the conditions defined in a workflow,
a workflow execution is created and assigned with an identifier. The workflow execution
is bound to the realm resource associated with the event, and only a single instance of a workflow can be active for that
realm resource at any given time.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A realm resource can be any entity within the realm, such as a user, client, group, or a role.
At the moment, workflows can be defined for the following realm resources:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Users</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Once a workflow is active for a realm resource, its step chain is processed. The steps run sequentially, and they will
run immediately or be scheduled to execute later in time, depending on each step configuration.
Once all the steps are executed, the workflow execution is completed and the realm resource
is no longer bound to that workflow.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>That is the main gist of Keycloak Workflows. There are more details and settings that can be
configured to customize the behavior and the lifecycle of a workflow, how their instances are created, managed,
and bound to realm resources, as well as how their steps are executed.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_understanding_workflow_definition_"><a class="anchor" href="#_understanding_workflow_definition_"></a>Understanding the workflow definition</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/workflows/understanding-workflow-definition.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/understanding-workflow-definition.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/understanding-workflow-definition.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph _abstract">
<p>Workflows are defined in YAML format. This format allows for a clear and human-readable way to specify the automation process
represented by a workflow.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In its simplest form, a workflow definition can be defined as follows:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="yaml"><span class="key">name</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">Onboarding new users</span></span>
<span class="key">on</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">user-created</span></span>
<span class="key">steps</span>:
  - <span class="string"><span class="content">uses: notify-user</span></span>
    <span class="key">with</span>:
      <span class="key">message</span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">|</span><span class="content">
        <p>Dear ${user.firstName} ${user.lastName}, </p>

        <p>Welcome to ${realm.displayName}!</p>

        <p>
           Best regards,<br/>
           ${realm.displayName} Team
        </p></span></span>
  - <span class="string"><span class="content">uses: add-required-action</span></span>
    <span class="key">after</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">30d</span></span>
    <span class="key">with</span>:
      <span class="key">action</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">UPDATE_PASSWORD</span></span>
  - <span class="string"><span class="content">uses: restart</span></span>
    <span class="key">with</span>:
      <span class="key">position</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">1</span></span></code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The example above is very simple but illustrates the core structure and the flexibility of a workflow to automate administrative tasks.
It is composed of three main sections:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>name</code>: A unique and user-friendly name to identify the workflow within the realm.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>on</code>: The event that will trigger the workflow. In this case, the workflow is triggered when a new user is added to the realm.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>steps</code>: A set of one or more steps to be executed when executing a workflow execution. In this example, three steps are defined:</p>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>The first step uses the built-in <code>notify-user</code> action to send a welcome message to the new user.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>The second step uses the built-in <code>add-required-action</code> action to require the user to update their password after 30 days.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>The third step uses the built-in <code>restart</code> action to restart the workflow from the second step so that the user is forced to update their password every 30 days.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Here is a more detailed look at all settings available from the workflow definition:</p>
</div>
<div class="dlist">
<dl>
<dt class="hdlist1"><code>name</code></dt>
<dd>
<p>A unique and user-friendly name to identify the workflow within the realm.
This name is crucial for management and logging purposes.
This setting is mandatory.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1"><code>on</code></dt>
<dd>
<p>Define a condition that determines the event that will trigger the workflow.
The condition is written using an expression language that supports a variety of checks on the event.
See <a href="#_workflow_events_">Triggering workflows on events</a> for more details.
This setting is optional.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1"><code>schedule</code></dt>
<dd>
<p>Define a schedule that will trigger the workflow at defined intervals.
See <a href="#_scheduling_workflows_">Scheduling workflows</a> for more details.
This setting is optional.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1"><code>if</code></dt>
<dd>
<p>Define a condition that must be met for the workflow to be triggered.
The condition is written using an expression language that supports a variety of checks on the realm resource
associated with the event.
A workflow execution is only created if the expression evaluates to <code>true</code>.
If this setting is omitted, the event defined in the <code>on</code> setting will always create the workflow execution.
See <a href="#_workflow_conditions_">Defining conditions</a> for more details.
This setting is optional.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1"><code>steps</code></dt>
<dd>
<p>Define the step chain consisting of one or more steps to be sequentially executed during the lifetime of a workflow.
See <a href="#_workflow_steps_">Defining steps</a> for more details.
This setting is mandatory.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1"><code>concurrency</code></dt>
<dd>
<p>This setting controls the behavior when multiple events that would trigger the same workflow occur for the same realm resource while a workflow execution is already active for that resource. This setting is optional.
+ The available options are:</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>restart-in-progress</code>: A new event causes the current workflow execution to restart from the beginning.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>cancel-in-progress</code>: A new event causes the current workflow execution to be canceled and disassociated from the realm resource.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1"><code>enabled</code></dt>
<dd>
<p>This setting enables or disables the workflow. If set to <code>false</code>, new workflow executions will not be created for the workflow and any active workflow execution will be paused.
This setting is optional and defaults to <code>true</code>.</p>
</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_workflow_expression_language_"><a class="anchor" href="#_workflow_expression_language_"></a>Understanding the workflow expression language</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/workflows/understanding-workflow-expression.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/understanding-workflow-expression.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/understanding-workflow-expression.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Some settings from the workflow definition can be defined using a boolean expression language, the Workflow Expression Language.
Expressions are defined using functions, operands, and logical operators. The functions available in an expression will
depend on the setting where it is being defined.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The functions can have zero or more arguments, and they can be combined with the following logical operators and symbols to define
complex expressions:</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%;">
<col style="width: 50%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Operator</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>and</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Logical <code>AND</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>or</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Logical <code>OR</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>not</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Logical <code>NOT</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>()</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Grouping and delimiting conditional logic</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>These examples are all valid expressions:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="yaml"><span class="error">f1</span>
<span class="error">f1 and f2</span>
<span class="error">not (f1 and f2)</span>
<span class="error">(f1 and f2) or f3</span></code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The settings that supports expressions provide its own set of functions as you will see in the following sections.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_managing_workflows_"><a class="anchor" href="#_managing_workflows_"></a>Managing workflows</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/workflows/managing-workflows.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/managing-workflows.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/managing-workflows.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph _abstract">
<p>Workflows can be managed through the Admin Console or the Admin REST API.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Only realm administrators with the appropriate permissions can manage workflows as they are considered sensitive operations.
For more details, see <a href="#_understanding_different_types_realm_admins_">Understanding different types of Realm Admins</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="managing-workflows-through-the-admin-console"><a class="anchor" href="#managing-workflows-through-the-admin-console"></a>Managing workflows through the Admin Console</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To manage workflows through the Admin Console, you can follow these steps:</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Workflows</strong> in the menu.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<div class="title">Empty workflows list</div>
<p><span class="image"><img src="./images/workflows-empty-list.png" alt="Empty workflows list"></span></p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If your realm does not have any workflows defined yet, you will see an empty list. To create a new workflow, click <strong>Create</strong>.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Creating a new workflow
<span class="image"><img src="./images/workflows-create.png" alt="Creating a new workflow"></span></p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This will open the workflow creation screen where you can define the workflow using YAML format. To save the workflow, click <strong>Save</strong>.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Once you have created one or more workflows, they will be listed in the workflows list.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<div class="title">List of workflows</div>
<p><span class="image"><img src="./images/workflows-list.png" alt="List of workflows"></span></p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>From the workflows list, you can perform the following actions:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Create</strong>: Click <strong>Create workflow</strong> to create a new workflow.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Update</strong>: Click on the name of an existing workflow to update it.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Enable/Disable</strong>: Use the toggle button on the <strong>Status</strong> column to enable or disable a workflow.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Copy</strong>: Click on the <strong>Copy</strong> button next to a workflow to create a copy of it. This is useful if you want to create a new workflow based on an existing one.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Delete</strong>: Click on the <strong>Delete</strong> button next to a workflow to delete it.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="updating-a-workflow"><a class="anchor" href="#updating-a-workflow"></a>Updating a workflow</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To update a workflow, click on its name in the workflows list. This will open the workflow in edit mode, where you can modify its YAML definition.
After making your changes, click <strong>Save</strong> to apply the updates.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>There are limitations when updating workflows if they have scheduled steps. In such cases, you are not able to change the step chain of a workflow
if there are active instances of the workflow being updated. This limitation is in place to ensure the integrity of ongoing workflow instances
where updates to the step chain could lead to an expensive operation of migrating existing instances to the new step chain,
which could impact system performance as well as lead to inconsistencies and an unexpected behavior.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In future releases, we plan to introduce a more flexible approach to updating workflows with scheduled steps, so that administrators
are going to be allowed to migrate realm resources scheduled for a specific step to a different step in the updated workflow.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For now, the only option is to either wait for all active instances to complete or to delete the workflow and create a new one.
Note that deleting a workflow will also delete all its active instances, therefore, realm resources associated with those instances
will not be processed further, and they would need to be re-associated with a new workflow instance if needed.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_workflow_events_"><a class="anchor" href="#_workflow_events_"></a>Triggering workflows on events</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/workflows/listening-workflow-events.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/listening-workflow-events.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/listening-workflow-events.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The <code>on</code> setting defines the event that will trigger the workflow. You should choose the event accordingly to the realm resource and the intent
of the workflow.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The value of the `on' setting is an expression that must evaluate to true. In its basic form, the expression is simply
the name of the event.</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="yaml"><span class="key">on</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">user-created</span></span></code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>As you can see, events are functions in an expression and, as such, they also support parameters to provide more specific conditions.
For example, to trigger a workflow when a user is added to a specific group, you can use the following expression:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="yaml"><span class="key">on</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">user-group-membership-added(/mygroup)</span></span></code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can also combine multiple conditions using logical operators. For example, to trigger a workflow when a user is created or when they authenticate, you can use:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="yaml"><span class="key">on</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">user-created or user-authenticated</span></span></code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Even though the <code>on</code> setting can be defined using expressions, keep in mind that a single event triggers a workflow.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If this setting is not specified, the workflow will not be triggered by any event, but workflow
executions can still be created manually for a specific realm resource.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>At the moment, workflows support event functions for the following realm resources:</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_workflow_event_functions_"><a class="anchor" href="#_workflow_event_functions_"></a>Event functions</h4>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">

</colgroup>

<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Parameters</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>user-created</code></p></td>

</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_scheduling_workflows_"><a class="anchor" href="#_scheduling_workflows_"></a>Scheduling workflows</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/workflows/scheduling-workflows.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/scheduling-workflows.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/scheduling-workflows.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Workflows can be scheduled to run periodically according to a defined interval. This is done using the <code>schedule</code> setting
in the workflow definition.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A key difference between event-based triggering and scheduled workflows is that scheduled workflows follows a passive execution model
where the workflow engine periodically checks for realm resources that meet the defined condition.</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="yaml"><span class="key">name</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">Track inactive users</span></span>
<span class="key">schedule</span>:
  <span class="key">after</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">5s</span></span>
  <span class="key">batch-size</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">100</span></span></code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This method of scheduling is useful for automating tasks that need to be performed regularly, such as cleaning up inactive
users or enforcing specific policies on realm resources. It is an alternative to event-based triggering, but it can also
be used in combination with it. When used together, the workflow will be triggered either by the defined event or by the schedule.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When a workflow is scheduled, it will be triggered automatically at the defined interval. At each run, the workflow engine
will query for the realm resources that matches the workflow’s condition and will create a workflow execution for each of them,
up to the defined batch size. If no condition is defined, the workflow will be executed for all realm resources of the type associated
with the workflow. In the example above, the workflow is scheduled to run every 5 seconds and will process up to 100 realm resources at each run.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The <code>schedule</code> setting supports the following parameters:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>after</code>: Defines the interval between each run of the workflow.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>batch-size</code>: Defines the maximum number of realm resources to process at each run.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_workflow_conditions_"><a class="anchor" href="#_workflow_conditions_"></a>Defining conditions</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/workflows/defining-conditions.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/defining-conditions.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/defining-conditions.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The optional <code>if</code> setting allows you to define the conditions, as expressions, that the target resource must meet in
order for the workflow to be triggered. See <a href="#_workflow_expression_language_">Understanding the workflow expression language</a> for more details.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Conditions provide fine-grained control over whether a workflow execution should be created.
They allow you to inspect the context of the event and the state of the resource.
For example, you can create conditions to check:
* If a user has a specific attribute.
* If a specific role is granted to a user or if the user is joining a specific group.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If the condition evaluates to <code>true</code>, the workflow execution is created. If it evaluates to <code>false</code>, no workflow execution is created, even though
the expression from the <code>on</code> setting evaluates to <code>true</code>.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Just like the <code>on</code> setting, the condition is written using an expression that supports a variety of checks on the realm resource associated with the event.
For instance, considering a <code>user_created</code> event, you can define a condition to trigger the workflow only if the user has a specific attribute:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="yaml"><span class="key">on</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">user-created</span></span>
<span class="key">if</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">has-user-attribute(plan=gold)</span></span></code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In this example, the workflow will only be triggered when a new user is created and that user has an attribute <code>plan</code> with the value <code>gold</code>.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Keycloak provides a set of built-in conditions that you can use in your workflows.
The conditions are also based on the realm resource associated with the event.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_workflow_user_functions_"><a class="anchor" href="#_workflow_user_functions_"></a>User functions</h4>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33.3333%;">
<col style="width: 33.3333%;">
<col style="width: 33.3334%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Condition</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Parameters</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>has-user-attribute</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">If the user has an attribute set.</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The attribute name and optionally the attribute value using a properties format. If multiple values, they should be separated by comma. If the value is omitted, only the presence of the attribute is checked.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>has-role</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">If the user is granted with a specific role</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The name of the role.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>has-identity-provider-link</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">If the user is linked to an identity provider.</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The alias of the identity provider.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>is-member-of</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">If the user is member of a specific group.</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The name or path of the group.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_workflow_steps_"><a class="anchor" href="#_workflow_steps_"></a>Defining steps</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/workflows/defining-steps.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/defining-steps.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/defining-steps.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The <code>steps</code> setting allows you to define the step chain, which is a sequence of actions to be executed during the lifetime of a workflow execution.
Each step represents a specific action that can be performed, such as sending a notification, updating user attributes, or interacting with external systems.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Each step in the step chain is defined using the following structure:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="yaml"><span class="key">steps</span>:
  - <span class="string"><span class="content">uses: <step></span></span>
    <span class="key">with</span>:
      <span class="error"><param></span>: <span class="error"><value></span>
      <span class="error">...</span>
    <span class="key">after</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content"><duration></span></span>
  <span class="error">...</span></code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In its simplest form, a step is defined using only the <code>uses</code> field:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="yaml"><span class="key">steps</span>:
  - <span class="string"><span class="content">uses: disable-user</span></span></code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>However, some steps also support additional settings to customize their behavior:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="yaml"><span class="key">steps</span>:
  - <span class="string"><span class="content">uses: notify-user</span></span>
    <span class="key">with</span>:
      <span class="key">message</span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">Welcome to the platform!</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span></code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Here is a more detailed look at all fields available from defining a step:</p>
</div>
<div class="dlist">
<dl>
<dt class="hdlist1"><code>uses</code></dt>
<dd>
<p>The name of the step to be executed. This field is mandatory.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1"><code>with</code></dt>
<dd>
<p>Key/value pairs to be passed to the step. The available parameters depend on the step being used. This field is optional.</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1"><code>after</code></dt>
<dd>
<p>An optional duration to wait before executing the step. The duration is defined using a number followed by a time unit:</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>ms</code>: milliseconds</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>s</code>: seconds (default if no unit is specified)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>m</code>: minutes</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>h</code>: hours</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>d</code>: days</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</dd>
</dl>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In addition, ISO-8601 duration format is also supported, for example: <code>P1DT2H</code> (1 day and 2 hours). If no time unit is specified,
it assumes seconds by default.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Keycloak provides a set of built-in steps that you can use in your workflows. The steps are targeted at performing actions
on the realm resource associated with the event, so that each realm resource type has its own set of steps.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_workflow_user_steps_"><a class="anchor" href="#_workflow_user_steps_"></a>User steps</h4>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33.3333%;">
<col style="width: 33.3333%;">
<col style="width: 33.3334%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Step</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Configuration</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>add-required-action</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Add a required action to the user</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>action</code>: The name of the required action</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>remove-required-action</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Remove a required action from the user</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>action</code>: The name of the required action</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>grant-role</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Grant one or more roles to the user</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>role</code>: One or more role names to grant. This can be a single value or a list of values (e.g., <code>[value1, value2]</code>)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>revoke-role</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Revoke one or more roles from the user</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>role</code>: One or more role names to revoke. This can be a single value or a list of values (e.g., <code>[value1, value2]</code>)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>join-group</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Add the user to one or more groups</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>group</code>: One or more group names or paths to join. This can be a single value or a list of values (e.g., <code>[value1, value2]</code>)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>leave-group</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Remove the user from one or more groups</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>group</code>: One or more group names or paths to leave. This can be a single value or a list of values (e.g., <code>[value1, value2]</code>)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>set-user-attribute</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Set one or more attributes on the user. Allows providing multiple <code><name></code>/<code><value></code> pairs</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code><name></code>: The attribute name</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code><value></code>: The value of the attribute</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>remove-user-attribute</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Remove one or more attributes from the user</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>attribute</code>: One or more attribute names to remove. This can be a single value or a list of values (e.g., <code>[value1, value2]</code>)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>notify-user</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Notify the user by email</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>subject</code>: The email subject</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>message</code>: The email message in plain text or HTML format</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>to</code>: The recipient email address. If not provided, the user’s email address will be used</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>unlink-user</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Unlink the user from one or more external Identity Providers</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>idp</code>: One or more Identity Provider aliases to unlink. This can be:</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Single value</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>List of values (e.g., <code>[value1, value2]</code>)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>*</code> to unlink user from all linked Identity Providers</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>disable-user</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Disable the user</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">None</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>delete-user</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Delete the user</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">None</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>invite-user</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Send an invitation email with an action token link to the user</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>actions</code>: Required action names the user must complete. Defaults to <code>UPDATE_PASSWORD</code> and <code>VERIFY_EMAIL</code>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>client-id</code>: Client id associated with the action token. Defaults to the realm’s system client.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>redirect-uri</code>: Where to redirect the user after completing the required actions. Requires <code>client-id</code>.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The <code>invite-user</code> step builds invitation links from the configured hostname, resolved from the realm <code>frontendUrl</code> attribute or the <code>--hostname</code> option when it is set to a full URL. Because the step runs on a background thread without an active request, one of these must be configured: a workflow containing an <code>invite-user</code> step is rejected at creation time with a <code>400 Bad Request</code> if none is set. The step is only skipped at runtime if the hostname configuration is removed after the workflow was created.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_workflow_client_steps_"><a class="anchor" href="#_workflow_client_steps_"></a>Client steps</h4>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33.3333%;">
<col style="width: 33.3333%;">
<col style="width: 33.3334%;">
</colgroup>

<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Step</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Configuration</th>

<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>disable-client</code></p></td>

<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_workflow_immediate_steps_"><a class="anchor" href="#_workflow_immediate_steps_"></a>Understanding immediate steps</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A step can run immediately whenever it is reached in the step chain. A immediate step is executed as soon as the previous step is completed,
without any delay. This is the default behavior for steps in a workflow.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For example, in the following workflow definition, both steps are immediate steps:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="yaml"><span class="key">steps</span>:
  - <span class="string"><span class="content">uses: notify-user</span></span>
  - <span class="string"><span class="content">uses: disable-user</span></span></code></pre>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="understanding-scheduled-steps"><a class="anchor" href="#understanding-scheduled-steps"></a>Understanding scheduled steps</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A step can be scheduled to run after a specific duration using the <code>after</code> field. A scheduled step is executed after waiting for the defined duration
once the previous step is completed.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For example, in the following workflow definition, the <code>disable-user</code> step is a scheduled step that will run 7 days after notifying the user:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="yaml"><span class="key">steps</span>:
  - <span class="string"><span class="content">uses: notify-user</span></span>
  - <span class="string"><span class="content">uses: disable-user</span></span>
    <span class="key">after</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">7d</span></span></code></pre>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_understanding_workflows_engine_"><a class="anchor" href="#_understanding_workflows_engine_"></a>Understanding the workflows engine</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/workflows/understanding-workflows-engine.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/understanding-workflows-engine.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/understanding-workflows-engine.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph _abstract">
<p>The lifecycle and execution of workflows in Keycloak is managed by the Workflows Engine.
The engine is responsible for processing events, creating workflow executions, and processing their steps.
Once a workflow execution is created, the engine takes over and manages the execution of its steps chain.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The execution of the steps chain is done asynchronously and detached from the request that originated the event that
triggered the workflow. This means that workflows are not scheduled nor executed immediately within the context of the request,
but rather sent to a task thread pool and scheduled to be executed later by the engine. This allows for better performance and scalability, as the steps can be executed
in the background without blocking the main request thread.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For immediate steps, the engine processes them as soon as the workflow execution is submitted to the task thread pool. This means that immediate steps are executed
right away, as soon as the workflow execution is picked up by a worker thread from the pool.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For scheduled steps, the engine continuously monitors the state of all active workflow executions in the realm. This is done by a background
task that runs periodically to check for any workflow executions that have steps ready to be executed. The schedule steps of a workflow are also executed asynchronously
by the background task, using the same task thread pool as immediate steps.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="configuring-the-scheduled-steps-execution-interval"><a class="anchor" href="#configuring-the-scheduled-steps-execution-interval"></a>Configuring the scheduled steps execution interval</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>By default, the background task tracking due steps runs every 12 hours, but this interval can be configured by setting the following server configuration option:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>spi-events-listener—​workflow-event-listener—​step-runner-task-interval</code>: Defines the interval at which the background task runs to check for workflow steps that are due for execution.
It follows the same format used in the workflow step <code>after</code> field, where you can specify the interval as a number followed by a time unit (<code>ms</code>, <code>s</code> - default, <code>m</code>, <code>h</code>, <code>d</code>) or using the ISO-8601 duration format.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>By default, the first execution of the background task occurs after one full interval has elapsed since the server started.
You can control this by setting a start time that acts as an anchor for aligning executions to a predictable schedule:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>spi-events-listener—​workflow-event-listener—​step-runner-task-start-time</code>: Defines the time of day used to align the background task executions, in <code>HH:mm</code> format (e.g., <code>02:00</code>, <code>14:30</code>), using the server’s local timezone.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When a start time is set, the task interval is aligned to a grid of execution times anchored at the specified time. For example, with a start time of <code>02:00</code> and an interval of <code>12h</code>, the task always runs at 02:00 and 14:00 regardless of when the server was started. If the server starts at 10:30, the first execution would occur at 14:00.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can adjust these options based on your realm’s needs and the expected frequency of workflow executions.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="configuring-the-task-execution-timeout"><a class="anchor" href="#configuring-the-task-execution-timeout"></a>Configuring the task execution timeout</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Most of the time, steps are executed in a short amount of time. However, there might be cases where a step takes longer
to execute due to various reasons, such as network latency depending on an external service delays, or complex processing logic.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>By default, the timeout for executing a workflow is set to <strong>5 seconds</strong>. The amount of steps that are processed in a single run
depends on the number of immediate steps that are defined in the workflow, as they are executed sequentially in the same run. Once
the workflow encounters a scheduled step, it schedules the step and terminates the execution.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If a workflow execution takes longer than the defined timeout, the engine will fail the current step, and it will attempt
to run this step in the next execution of the workflow. This is done to prevent long-running executions from blocking the workflow task thread pool
and impacting the execution of other workflows.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can configure the timeout for the workflow executor task by setting the following server configuration option:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>spi-workflow—​default—​executor-task-timeout</code>: Defines the timeout for executing a workflow. It follows the same format
used in the workflow step <code>after</code> field, where you can specify the interval as a number followed by a time unit (<code>ms</code>, <code>s</code> - default, <code>m</code>, <code>h</code>, <code>d</code>)
or using the ISO-8601 duration format.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="performance-considerations-2"><a class="anchor" href="#performance-considerations-2"></a>Performance considerations</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Workflows can introduce additional processing overhead. This is mainly true when workflows are triggered frequently
such as when users are authenticating. Even though workflows are scheduled and executed asynchronously, they still consume
system resources. Therefore, it’s important to monitor the performance of your realm and adjust your workflow definitions
accordingly to ensure optimal performance.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Consider the following best practices when defining workflows:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Keep workflows simple and focused on specific tasks and avoid long-running transactions when executing steps in a workflow.
This is specially true for steps that are executed immediately upon workflow execution creation.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Consider using short timeouts for the step execution to avoid blocking the workflow execution for too long and potentially
exhaust the workflow task thread pool and impacting the execution of other workflows.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Adjust the background task interval based on the expected frequency of workflow executions in your realm. If your realm has a high volume of workflow executions,
consider reducing the interval to avoid processing multiple workflows at once.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_handling_failures_"><a class="anchor" href="#_handling_failures_"></a>Handling failures</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/workflows/handling-failures.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/handling-failures.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/handling-failures.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph _abstract">
<p>The workflows engine keeps track of the execution process by storing the step that should run in a state table. If
the step fails to run, either due to an error in the step execution or because of a timeout, the error is logged, an event
is fired, and the state table remains unchanged. This effectively means that the step will be retried the next time the workflow
execution task runs.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In this initial version there’s no limit to the number of retries, so a workflow execution can get stuck until the administrator
intervenes and either fixes the issue that is preventing the step from running successfully or uses the API to cancel the workflow
execution or to migrate the resource to a different workflow/step. Thus, it is important that admins monitor the workflow execution
logs and check for any errors that may occur repeatedly.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
