<td class="content">
The state table is used even for immediate steps (i.e. steps that are supposed to run immediately after the previous step).
This means that if an immediate step fails, the workflow execution will be retried later, and the failed step will be retried as well,
behaving as if it were a scheduled step. This is to ensure that the workflow execution process is consistent and that all steps are
retried in the same way, regardless of their configuration. This also ensures the workflow will be resumed in case of server restarts or crashes.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Future versions of the workflows engine will include more features to handle failures, such as the ability to configure a maximum number
of retries for each step, as well as the ability to define custom error handling logic for specific steps, like skip the step or cancel
the workflow execution.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_workflow_provider_events_"><a class="anchor" href="#_workflow_provider_events_"></a>Listening to workflow provider events</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/workflows/listening-workflow-provider-events.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/listening-workflow-provider-events.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/listening-workflow-provider-events.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>During the lifecycle of a workflow execution, Keycloak fires a series of provider events that represent key moments
such as activation, step execution, failures, and completion. SPI developers can listen to these events by implementing
the <code>ProviderEventListener</code> interface and registering the listener with the <code>KeycloakSessionFactory</code>.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Keycloak does not persist workflow execution history. By default, only log messages record what happened during
a workflow run (see <a href="#_troubleshooting_workflows_">Troubleshooting workflows</a>). Provider events allow you to capture and store workflow lifecycle
data externally — for example, in an audit database or monitoring system — providing a complete execution trail beyond
what the standard log messages offer.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="common-event-fields"><a class="anchor" href="#common-event-fields"></a>Common event fields</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>All workflow provider events extend the <code>WorkflowProviderEvent</code> interface, which provides the following common fields:</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%;">
<col style="width: 50%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Method</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>getKeycloakSession()</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The <code>KeycloakSession</code> associated with this event.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>getRealm()</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The realm where the workflow event occurred.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>getWorkflowId()</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The ID of the workflow.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>getWorkflowName()</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The name of the workflow.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>getResourceId()</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The ID of the resource (user or client) associated with the workflow.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>getResourceType()</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The type of the resource — either <code>USERS</code> or <code>CLIENTS</code>.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>getExecutionId()</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The unique ID for this workflow execution.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_workflow_provider_event_types_"><a class="anchor" href="#_workflow_provider_event_types_"></a>Event types</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The following event types are available:</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33.3333%;">
<col style="width: 33.3333%;">
<col style="width: 33.3334%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Event Type</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Additional Fields</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>WorkflowActivatedEvent</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Fired when a workflow is activated for a resource — either through a trigger event, a schedule, or a manual API call.</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>getTriggerEventType()</code>: The event provider ID that triggered activation (e.g., <code>user-created</code>, <code>scheduled</code>, or <code>AD_HOC</code> for manual activation).</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>WorkflowDeactivatedEvent</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Fired when a workflow execution is deactivated for a resource — for example, through a manual API call, a cancel-in-progress trigger, or because the resource no longer meets the workflow conditions.</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>getReason()</code>: The reason for deactivation.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>WorkflowRestartedEvent</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Fired when a workflow execution is restarted from the beginning for a resource.</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">None — uses only the common fields.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>WorkflowStepScheduledEvent</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Fired when a workflow step is scheduled for future execution (i.e., the step has an <code>after</code> delay).</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>getStepId()</code>: The ID of the scheduled step.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>getStepProviderId()</code>: The provider ID of the step (e.g., <code>disable-user</code>).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>getScheduledTime()</code>: The time the step is scheduled to execute, in milliseconds since epoch.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>getDelay()</code>: The delay duration string (e.g., <code>PT5M</code> for 5 minutes).</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>WorkflowStepExecutedEvent</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Fired when a workflow step completes successfully.</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>getStepId()</code>: The ID of the executed step.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>getStepProviderId()</code>: The provider ID of the step.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>WorkflowStepFailedEvent</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Fired when a workflow step execution fails.</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>getStepId()</code>: The ID of the failed step.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>getStepProviderId()</code>: The provider ID of the step.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>getErrorMessage()</code>: The error message from the failure.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>WorkflowResourceMigratedEvent</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Fired when resources are migrated from one workflow (or step) to another using the migration API.</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>getSourceWorkflowId()</code> / <code>getSourceWorkflowName()</code>: The source workflow.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>getDestinationWorkflowId()</code> / <code>getDestinationWorkflowName()</code>: The destination workflow.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>getSourceStepId()</code> / <code>getSourceStepProviderId()</code>: The source step.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>getDestinationStepId()</code> / <code>getDestinationStepProviderId()</code>: The destination step.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>getOldExecutionId()</code> / <code>getNewExecutionId()</code>: The execution IDs from the source and destination workflows.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>WorkflowCompletedEvent</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Fired when all steps of a workflow have been executed successfully and the workflow execution is complete.</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">None — uses only the common fields.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="event-lifecycle"><a class="anchor" href="#event-lifecycle"></a>Event lifecycle</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>During a typical workflow execution, provider events are fired in the following order:</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p><code>WorkflowActivatedEvent</code> — the workflow is activated for the resource.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>For each step in the step chain:</p>
<div class="olist loweralpha">
<ol class="loweralpha" type="a">
<li>
<p><code>WorkflowStepScheduledEvent</code> — if the step has an <code>after</code> delay.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>WorkflowStepExecutedEvent</code> — when the step completes successfully.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>WorkflowStepFailedEvent</code> — if the step fails (replaces <code>WorkflowStepExecutedEvent</code>).</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>WorkflowCompletedEvent</code> — all steps completed successfully.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A <code>WorkflowDeactivatedEvent</code> may replace <code>WorkflowCompletedEvent</code> if the workflow is cancelled or the resource no longer
meets the workflow conditions. A <code>WorkflowRestartedEvent</code> may occur at any point if the workflow is restarted from the beginning
by a restart-in-progress trigger.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="implementing-a-listener"><a class="anchor" href="#implementing-a-listener"></a>Implementing a listener</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To listen to workflow provider events, create a custom <code>EventListenerProviderFactory</code> that registers a <code>ProviderEventListener</code>
with the <code>KeycloakSessionFactory</code> during initialization. The listener is packaged as a JAR and deployed to the <code>providers/</code> folder,
then enabled in the Admin Console under <strong>Realm Settings</strong> → <strong>Events</strong> → <strong>Event listeners</strong>.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The following example shows a factory that registers a listener to capture workflow events:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="java"><span class="keyword">import</span> <span class="include">org.keycloak.events.EventListenerProvider</span>;
<span class="keyword">import</span> <span class="include">org.keycloak.events.EventListenerProviderFactory</span>;
<span class="keyword">import</span> <span class="include">org.keycloak.models.KeycloakSession</span>;
<span class="keyword">import</span> <span class="include">org.keycloak.models.KeycloakSessionFactory</span>;
<span class="keyword">import</span> <span class="include">org.keycloak.models.workflow.WorkflowProviderEvent</span>;
<span class="keyword">import</span> <span class="include">org.keycloak.models.workflow.WorkflowProviderEvent.WorkflowStepFailedEvent</span>;

<span class="directive">public</span> <span class="type">class</span> <span class="class">WorkflowAuditListenerFactory</span> <span class="directive">implements</span> EventListenerProviderFactory {

    <span class="annotation">@Override</span>
    <span class="directive">public</span> EventListenerProvider create(KeycloakSession session) {
        <span class="keyword">return</span> <span class="keyword">new</span> WorkflowAuditListener(session);
    }

    <span class="annotation">@Override</span>
    <span class="directive">public</span> <span class="type">void</span> postInit(KeycloakSessionFactory factory) {
        factory.register(event -> {
            <span class="keyword">if</span> (event <span class="keyword">instanceof</span> WorkflowStepFailedEvent failedEvent) {
                <span class="comment">// handle step failure — e.g., send a notification or store in an audit log</span>
                <span class="predefined-type">String</span> workflowName = failedEvent.getWorkflowName();
                <span class="predefined-type">String</span> stepId = failedEvent.getStepId();
                <span class="predefined-type">String</span> error = failedEvent.getErrorMessage();
                <span class="comment">// ...</span>
            } <span class="keyword">else</span> <span class="keyword">if</span> (event <span class="keyword">instanceof</span> WorkflowProviderEvent workflowEvent) {
                <span class="comment">// handle other workflow events</span>
                <span class="predefined-type">String</span> workflowName = workflowEvent.getWorkflowName();
                <span class="predefined-type">String</span> resourceId = workflowEvent.getResourceId();
                <span class="comment">// ...</span>
            }
        });
    }

    <span class="annotation">@Override</span>
    <span class="directive">public</span> <span class="type">void</span> init(org.keycloak.Config.Scope config) {
    }

    <span class="annotation">@Override</span>
    <span class="directive">public</span> <span class="type">void</span> close() {
    }

    <span class="annotation">@Override</span>
    <span class="directive">public</span> <span class="predefined-type">String</span> getId() {
        <span class="keyword">return</span> <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">workflow-audit</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>;
    }
}</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The factory must be registered as a service provider in <code>META-INF/services/org.keycloak.events.EventListenerProviderFactory</code>
so that Keycloak discovers it when the JAR is deployed.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="use-cases"><a class="anchor" href="#use-cases"></a>Use cases</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Since Keycloak does not persist workflow execution history, provider events are the primary mechanism for building
a complete audit trail of workflow activity. Common use cases include:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Auditing and compliance</strong>: Store workflow events in an external database to maintain a full record of workflow executions, step results, and failures.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>External notifications</strong>: Send alerts (e.g., via email or messaging systems) when specific events occur, such as step failures or workflow completion.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Monitoring and metrics</strong>: Feed workflow event data into monitoring systems to track execution rates, failure rates, and step durations.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_troubleshooting_workflows_"><a class="anchor" href="#_troubleshooting_workflows_"></a>Troubleshooting workflows</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/workflows/troubleshooting-workflows.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/troubleshooting-workflows.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/troubleshooting-workflows.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When workflows are not behaving as expected, server logs are the primary tool for understanding what is happening.
The workflow engine logs detailed information about workflow lifecycle events, step execution, and errors.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="enabling-workflow-debug-logging"><a class="anchor" href="#enabling-workflow-debug-logging"></a>Enabling workflow debug logging</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>By default, the workflow engine logs warnings and errors. To see the full execution flow, enable <code>DEBUG</code> level
logging for the <code>org.keycloak.models.workflow</code> category by setting the following server configuration option:</p>
</div>
<div class="literalblock">
<div class="content">
<pre>--log-level=org.keycloak.models.workflow:debug</pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This enables debug logging for the workflow engine, all step providers, and the workflow state provider.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="what-to-look-for-in-the-logs"><a class="anchor" href="#what-to-look-for-in-the-logs"></a>What to look for in the logs</h4>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="workflow-activation-and-scheduling"><a class="anchor" href="#workflow-activation-and-scheduling"></a>Workflow activation and scheduling</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When a workflow is triggered by an event, the engine logs the activation and scheduling of the first step:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>Workflow '<name>' activated for resource <id> (execution id: <id>)</code> — the workflow execution has been created and is being processed.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>Scheduled step <step> to run in <duration> for resource <id> (execution id: <id>)</code> — a scheduled step has been queued to run after the specified duration.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="step-execution"><a class="anchor" href="#step-execution"></a>Step execution</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>As steps are executed, the engine logs their progress:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>Running step <step> on resource <id> (execution id: <id>)</code> — a step is about to be executed.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>Step <step> completed successfully (execution id: <id>)</code> — the step finished without errors.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>Workflow '<name>' completed for resource <id> (execution id: <id>)</code> — all steps in the workflow have been executed.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="step-failures-and-timeouts"><a class="anchor" href="#step-failures-and-timeouts"></a>Step failures and timeouts</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When a step fails or the executor times out, the engine logs the error and fires a step failed event. The step will be
retried in the next execution cycle (see <a href="#_handling_failures_">Handling failures</a> for more details).</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>Step <step> failed (execution id: <id>) - error message: <message></code> — the step threw an exception during execution.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>Workflow executor timed out during execution of step <step></code> — runtime exception indicating that the step exceeded the configured executor task timeout. See <a href="#_understanding_workflows_engine_">Understanding the workflows engine</a> for how to configure the timeout.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>Workflow executor was cancelled during execution of step <step></code> — runtime exception indicating that the executor service was cancelled for a reason other than timeout.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="skipped-and-cancelled-workflows"><a class="anchor" href="#skipped-and-cancelled-workflows"></a>Skipped and cancelled workflows</h5>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>Skipping workflow <name> as it is disabled</code> — the workflow is disabled and will not process events.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>Workflow '<name>' cancelled for resource <id> (execution id: <id>)</code> — the workflow execution was cancelled.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>Resource <id> is no longer eligible for workflow <name>. Cancelling execution of the workflow.</code> — the resource no longer meets the workflow conditions upon resuming a scheduled step.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="workflow-errors"><a class="anchor" href="#workflow-errors"></a>Workflow errors</h5>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>Error processing event <event> for workflow <name>: <message></code> — an error occurred while processing the event that triggers the workflow.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>Error resuming workflow <name> for resource <id>: <message></code> — an error occurred while resuming a scheduled workflow execution.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>Could not find step <step> in workflow <name> for resource <id>. Cancelling execution of the workflow.</code> — the step scheduled to run could not be found in the workflow.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="step-level-warnings"><a class="anchor" href="#step-level-warnings"></a>Step-level warnings</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Individual step providers log warnings when configuration is missing or invalid. Examples include:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>Missing required configuration option '<key>' in <step></code> — a required parameter was not provided in the step’s <code>with</code> block.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>Invalid required action <action> configured in <step></code> — the required action name is not recognized.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>User <id> has no email address, skipping notification</code> — the <code>notify-user</code> step could not send an email.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>Failed to send notification email to <recipient></code> — an email delivery failure occurred.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="useful-log-categories"><a class="anchor" href="#useful-log-categories"></a>Useful log categories</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If you need more targeted logging, you can enable debug logging for specific components:</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%;">
<col style="width: 50%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Category</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>org.keycloak.models.workflow</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">All workflow-related logging (engine, steps, state)</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>org.keycloak.models.workflow.DefaultWorkflowProvider</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Workflow engine lifecycle (activation, conditions, event processing)</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>org.keycloak.models.workflow.RunWorkflowTask</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Step execution, completion, failures, and timeouts</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>org.keycloak.models.workflow.ScheduleWorkflowTask</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Step scheduling and delayed execution</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_workflow_security_considerations_"><a class="anchor" href="#_workflow_security_considerations_"></a>Security considerations</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/workflows/security-considerations.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/security-considerations.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/security-considerations.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When designing workflows, it is important to understand the trust boundaries between the event that triggers a workflow, the conditions that control
whether it runs, and the steps it executes. A misconfigured workflow can allow users to trigger privileged actions on themselves without
administrator involvement.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This section is particularly relevant when self-registration is enabled in the realm.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="attribute-based-conditions-and-privileged-steps"><a class="anchor" href="#attribute-based-conditions-and-privileged-steps"></a>Attribute-based conditions and privileged steps</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Conditions such as <code>has-user-attribute</code> evaluate attributes stored on the user. Steps such as <code>grant-role</code> and <code>join-group</code> perform privileged
actions on the same user. When these are combined, the security of the workflow depends entirely on <strong>who can write</strong> the attribute
that the condition checks.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Consider the following workflow:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="yaml"><span class="key">name</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">Onboarding gold members</span></span>
<span class="key">on</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">user-created</span></span>
<span class="key">if</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">has-user-attribute(membership=gold)</span></span>
<span class="key">steps</span>:
  - <span class="string"><span class="content">uses: grant-role</span></span>
    <span class="key">with</span>:
      <span class="key">role</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">gold-member</span></span></code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If the <code>membership</code> attribute is writable by end users - for example, through a registration form - then a self-registering user
can set <code>membership=gold</code>, satisfy the condition, and receive the <code>gold-member</code> role without any administrator review.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To use this workflow safely, the <code>membership</code> attribute must be configured so that only administrators can write to it. There are two aspects
to consider: managed vs. unmanaged attributes, and attribute write permissions.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="unmanaged-attributes"><a class="anchor" href="#unmanaged-attributes"></a>Unmanaged attributes</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When the <code>Unmanaged Attributes</code> policy in the realm settings is set to <code>Enabled</code>, Keycloak persists any attribute submitted during
registration, even if the attribute is not defined in the user profile configuration. This means a self-registering user can supply
arbitrary attribute names and values that may satisfy a workflow condition.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To prevent this, avoid setting the <code>Unmanaged Attributes</code> policy to <code>Enabled</code>. Prefer <code>Disabled</code> (the default) or <code>Admin can edit</code>, which
restrict unmanaged attribute handling to the administrative context.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="managed-attribute-write-permissions"><a class="anchor" href="#managed-attribute-write-permissions"></a>Managed attribute write permissions</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Even when unmanaged attributes are disabled, a managed attribute can still be writable by end users if its <code>Who can edit</code> permission includes
<code>User</code>. For attributes used in workflow conditions that trigger privileged steps, the <code>Who can edit</code> permission should be restricted to <code>Admin</code>
only.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can configure this in the Admin Console under <code>Realm Settings</code> > <code>User Profile</code> > <code>Attributes</code>. Select the attribute and set the
<code>Who can edit</code> permission to <code>Admin</code>.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>See the <a href="https://www.keycloak.org/docs/26.8.1/server_admin/#_understanding-managed-and-unmanaged-attributes">Understanding managed and unmanaged attributes</a> section
for more details on attribute policies and permissions.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="event-source-and-step-target"><a class="anchor" href="#event-source-and-step-target"></a>Event source and step target</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Workflows triggered by user-initiated events such as <code>user-created</code> execute with the triggering user as the target of every step. There is
no separation between the user who caused the event and the user who receives the action - the user who registers is the same user who gets
the role granted.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When self-registration is enabled, any attribute set by the user at registration time is already present when the <code>user-created</code> event fires
and the workflow condition is evaluated. The user controls the input that the condition checks, which is why the attributes referenced in
conditions with privileged steps must not be writable by end users, as described in the previous section.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
When self-registration is disabled and users are created exclusively through the Admin Console or the Admin API, the <code>user-created</code>
event is only triggered by administrator actions. In that case, the administrator controls the attribute values and the risk described
above does not apply.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_understanding_common_use_cases_"><a class="anchor" href="#_understanding_common_use_cases_"></a>Understanding common use cases</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/workflows/understanding-common-use-cases.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/understanding-common-use-cases.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/workflows/understanding-common-use-cases.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph _abstract">
<p>Workflows can be used to automate a wide range of administrative tasks within a realm. Here are some common use cases where workflows can be particularly beneficial:</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="user-onboarding"><a class="anchor" href="#user-onboarding"></a>User Onboarding</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When a new user is created, a workflow can automatically send a welcome email, and assign initial roles or groups to the user. This ensures that new users have the necessary access and information from the moment they join.</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="yaml"><span class="key">name</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">Onboarding gold members</span></span>
<span class="key">on</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">user-created</span></span>
<span class="key">if</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">has-user-attribute(membership=gold)</span></span>
<span class="key">steps</span>:
  - <span class="string"><span class="content">uses: notify-user</span></span>
    <span class="key">with</span>:
      <span class="key">message</span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">Welcome to the Gold Membership program!</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>
  - <span class="string"><span class="content">uses: grant-role</span></span>
    <span class="key">with</span>:
      <span class="key">role</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">gold-member</span></span></code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock warning">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-warning" title="Warning"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
When using attribute-based conditions with privileged steps like <code>grant-role</code> or <code>join-group</code>, ensure the attribute
is not writable by end users. See <a href="#_workflow_security_considerations_">Security considerations</a> for details.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="user-offboarding"><a class="anchor" href="#user-offboarding"></a>User Offboarding</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When a user is removed from a specific group, a workflow can automatically revoke certain roles or permissions associated with that group.</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="yaml"><span class="key">name</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">Offboarding sales members</span></span>
<span class="key">on</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">user-group-membership-removed(/Sales)</span></span>
<span class="key">steps</span>:
  - <span class="string"><span class="content">uses: revoke-role</span></span>
    <span class="key">with</span>:
      <span class="key">role</span>:
        - <span class="string"><span class="content">sales-rep</span></span>
        - <span class="string"><span class="content">manager</span></span>
        - <span class="string"><span class="content">sales-intern</span></span></code></pre>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="tracking-user-activity-and-taking-actions-on-inactivity"><a class="anchor" href="#tracking-user-activity-and-taking-actions-on-inactivity"></a>Tracking user activity and taking actions on inactivity</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When a user has been inactive for a certain period, a workflow can send reminder emails and deactivate the account.</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="yaml"><span class="key">name</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">Track inactive users</span></span>
<span class="key">on</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">user-authenticated</span></span>
<span class="key">schedule</span>:
  <span class="key">after</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">5s</span></span>
  <span class="key">batch-size</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">2</span></span>
<span class="key">concurrency</span>:
  <span class="key">restart-in-progress</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">true</span></span>
<span class="key">steps</span>:
  - <span class="string"><span class="content">uses: notify-user</span></span>
    <span class="key">after</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">180d</span></span>
    <span class="key">with</span>:
      <span class="key">message</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">It has been a while since your last login. We miss you!</span></span>
  - <span class="string"><span class="content">uses: notify-user</span></span>
    <span class="key">after</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">60d</span></span>
    <span class="key">with</span>:
      <span class="key">message</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">Your account will be disabled in ${workflow.daysUntilNextStep} days!</span></span>
  - <span class="string"><span class="content">uses: disable-user</span></span>
    <span class="key">after</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">7d</span></span>
  - <span class="string"><span class="content">uses: notify-user</span></span>
    <span class="key">with</span>:
      <span class="key">message</span>: <span class="string"><span class="content">Your account was disabled. Sorry to see you go.</span></span></code></pre>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect1">
<h2 id="_managing_scim"><a class="anchor" href="#_managing_scim"></a>Managing users and groups through SCIM</h2>
<div class="sectionbody">
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/assembly-managing-scim.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/assembly-managing-scim.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/assembly-managing-scim.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div id="scim-introduction_server_administration_guide" class="paragraph _abstract">
<p>SCIM (System for Cross-domain Identity Management) is a standard protocol designed to simplify identity management across
multiple systems and domains. Defined by <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7643">RFC 7643</a> (Core Schema) and
<a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7644">RFC 7644</a> (Protocol), SCIM provides a common set of REST APIs and schemas
for creating, reading, updating, and deleting identity resources such as users and groups. By adopting SCIM, organizations
can automate user provisioning and deprovisioning across their identity infrastructure using widely supported tooling and
libraries.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Keycloak supports SCIM APIs for managing users and groups within a realm. External systems such as identity governance
platforms, HR systems, or other identity providers can use these standardized APIs to provision and manage users in
Keycloak without relying on the proprietary Admin REST API.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In the current release, the SCIM implementation covers:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>User management</strong>: Create, read, update, patch, and delete user resources.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Group management</strong>: Create, read, update, patch, and delete group resources, including membership management.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Filtering and pagination</strong>: Search resources using SCIM filter expressions with support for pagination, subject to the constraints described in <a href="#_scim_filtering_resources">Filtering resources</a>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Schema extensions</strong>: Support for the Enterprise User extension (RFC 7643, Section 4.3) and custom schema extensions through User Profile attribute mapping.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Schema discovery</strong>: Endpoints for discovering supported schemas, resource types, and server capabilities.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The SCIM API is based on the same underlying user and group management functionality as the Admin REST API, ensuring
consistency in behavior and permissions. However, the SCIM API provides a standardized interface that can be easily
integrated with third-party tools and platforms that support SCIM.</p>
</div>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/scim/intro.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/scim/intro.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/scim/intro.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_enabling_scim_"><a class="anchor" href="#_enabling_scim_"></a>Enabling SCIM for a realm</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/scim/enabling-scim.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/scim/enabling-scim.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/scim/enabling-scim.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph _abstract">
<p>Once the feature is enabled on the server, you must also enable SCIM for each realm individually. This can be done through
the Admin Console or the Admin REST API.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="using-the-admin-console-2"><a class="anchor" href="#using-the-admin-console-2"></a>Using the Admin Console</h4>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Realm settings</strong> in the menu.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>On the <strong>General</strong> tab, locate the <strong>SCIM API</strong> toggle.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Set the toggle to <strong>On</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<div class="title">Enabling SCIM API in realm settings</div>
<p><span class="image"><img src="./images/scim-realm-settings.png" alt="Enabling SCIM API in realm settings"></span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="obtaining-the-scim-api-base-url"><a class="anchor" href="#obtaining-the-scim-api-base-url"></a>Obtaining the SCIM API base URL</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The SCIM API in Keycloak is exposed under the following base URL:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre>http://<host>:<port>/realms/<realm-name>/scim/v2</pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This base URL is used to construct the full URLs for the available SCIM endpoints:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>/ServiceProviderConfig</code></p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>/ResourceTypes</code></p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>/Schemas</code></p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>/Users</code></p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>/Groups</code></p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The SCIM API requires a bearer token with the appropriate permissions. See <a href="#_scim_accessing_endpoints_">Authorizing access to SCIM endpoints</a>
for details on how to set up a client and obtain an access token.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_scim_accessing_endpoints_"><a class="anchor" href="#_scim_accessing_endpoints_"></a>Accessing the SCIM endpoints</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/scim/accessing-endpoints.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/scim/accessing-endpoints.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/scim/accessing-endpoints.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph _abstract">
<p>All SCIM endpoints require authorization using an OAuth 2.0 Bearer Token.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Unauthorized requests receive a <code>401 Unauthorized</code> response. The bearer token must also have the appropriate permissions
to perform the requested operation.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Only confidential clients can access the SCIM endpoints. Public clients are not supported for SCIM API calls.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="setting-up-a-service-account-client"><a class="anchor" href="#setting-up-a-service-account-client"></a>Setting up a service account client</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To access the SCIM APIs programmatically, you typically create a confidential client with a service account in Keycloak.
This client obtains access tokens using the client credentials grant.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Clients</strong> in the menu and then click <strong>Create client</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Set the <strong>Client ID</strong> (for example, <code>scim-client</code>) and click <strong>Next</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Enable <strong>Client authentication</strong> and <strong>Service accounts roles</strong>, then click <strong>Save</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>On the <strong>Credentials</strong> tab, note the <strong>Client secret</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="assigning-permissions"><a class="anchor" href="#assigning-permissions"></a>Assigning permissions</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The service account associated with the client must be granted the appropriate realm management roles to access
SCIM resources. The required roles depend on the operations the client needs to perform.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock warning">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-warning" title="Warning"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
The <strong>Full Scope Allowed</strong> switch is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Do not enable it on
the SCIM client. Instead, explicitly configure the required role scope mappings as described below. See
<a href="#_role_scope_mappings">Role scope mappings</a> for details.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Clients</strong> in the menu, then select the client you created.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <strong>Client scopes</strong> tab, select the dedicated client scope for the client (for example, <code>scim-client-dedicated</code>), then click the <strong>Scope</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Set <strong>Full Scope Allowed</strong> to <strong>Off</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Assign role</strong>, then filter by clients and select the <code>realm-management</code> client.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Assign the required roles based on the operations the client needs to perform. This adds the roles to the client’s role scope mappings.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <strong>Service account roles</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Assign role</strong>, then filter by clients and select the <code>realm-management</code> client.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Assign the same roles assigned in the previous step.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Roles included in the access token are the intersection of the client’s role scope mappings and the service account’s
assigned roles. Both steps above are required. For more details, see <a href="#_service_accounts">Using a service account</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The SCIM API relies on the same <a href="#_admin_permissions">permission model</a> as the Keycloak Admin REST API. If a service account
already has the admin roles needed to manage users and groups through the Admin API, no additional configuration is
required to use the SCIM endpoints.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If fine-grained admin permissions are enabled for the realm, access to SCIM resources can be further
restricted on a per-resource basis. For example, a client could be granted permission to view only specific users
or groups. For more details, see <a href="#_fine_grained_permissions">Fine-grained admin permissions</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The following table summarizes the permissions required for each type of SCIM operation:</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 25%;">
<col style="width: 25%;">
<col style="width: 50%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Operation</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Required Role</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Create, update, delete users</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>manage-users</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Full management access to user resources.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Read users</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>view-users</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Read-only access to individual user resources.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Search users</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>query-users</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Ability to list and filter user resources.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Create, update, delete groups</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>manage-users</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Full management access to group resources.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Read groups</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>view-users</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Read-only access to individual group resources.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Search groups</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>query-groups</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Ability to list and filter group resources.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Access discovery endpoints</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>query-users</code> or <code>query-groups</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Read access to <code>/ServiceProviderConfig</code>, <code>/ResourceTypes</code>, and <code>/Schemas</code>. Any role that implies <code>query-users</code> or <code>query-groups</code> (such as <code>view-users</code> or <code>manage-users</code>) also grants access.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The minimum set of roles required for full access to the SCIM API is <code>manage-users</code>, which covers all user and group
management operations as well as access to discovery endpoints.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="configuring-the-token-audience"><a class="anchor" href="#configuring-the-token-audience"></a>Configuring the token audience</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The SCIM API validates that access tokens contain the correct audience (<code>aud</code>) claim. The expected audience
is the SCIM API base URL for the realm:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre>http://<host>:<port>/realms/<realm-name>/scim/v2</pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Tokens without this audience are rejected with a <code>401 Unauthorized</code> response.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To configure the audience, add an <strong>Audience</strong> protocol mapper to the client:</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Clients</strong> in the menu, then select the client you created.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <strong>Client scopes</strong> tab, then click the dedicated scope for the client (for example, <code>scim-client-dedicated</code>).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Configure a new mapper</strong>, then select <strong>Audience</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Set <strong>Name</strong> to a descriptive value (for example, <code>scim-audience</code>).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>In <strong>Included Custom Audience</strong>, enter the SCIM API base URL for your realm (for example, <code>http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2</code>).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Ensure <strong>Add to access token</strong> is enabled.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The audience value must match the SCIM API base URL exactly as seen by Keycloak, including the scheme, host, port,
and path. If Keycloak is running behind a reverse proxy, use the frontend URL configured through the hostname settings.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="obtaining-an-access-token"><a class="anchor" href="#obtaining-an-access-token"></a>Obtaining an access token</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To call the SCIM APIs, obtain an access token using the client credentials grant:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">ACCESS_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST \
  http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/protocol/openid-connect/token \
  -d "grant_type=client_credentials" \
  -d "client_id=scim-client" \
  -d "client_secret=your-client-secret" \
  | jq -r '.access_token')</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Then use the token in the <code>Authorization</code> header when calling the SCIM endpoints:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/scim+json"</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_scim_admin_resource_protection_"><a class="anchor" href="#_scim_admin_resource_protection_"></a>Protection of administrative resources</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/scim/admin-resource-protection.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/scim/admin-resource-protection.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/scim/admin-resource-protection.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph _abstract">
<p>Keycloak automatically protects administrative users and groups from being modified through the SCIM API.
This prevents external identity providers or SCIM clients from accidentally or maliciously altering accounts
and groups that have administrative privileges in the realm.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="why-this-protection-exists"><a class="anchor" href="#why-this-protection-exists"></a>Why this protection exists</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The SCIM API is designed for automated user and group synchronization with external identity providers.
Because SCIM clients typically operate with broad management permissions, a compromised or misconfigured client
could otherwise:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Delete or disable administrator accounts, locking out realm management.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Modify administrator credentials or attributes.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Add unauthorized users to groups that carry administrative roles, escalating their privileges.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Remove administrators from their groups, revoking their access.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To prevent these scenarios, Keycloak ensures that administrative resources can only be managed through the
Admin Console or the Admin REST API, never through SCIM.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="protected-admin-users"><a class="anchor" href="#protected-admin-users"></a>Protected admin users</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A user is considered an administrative user if they hold any administrative role. This includes roles from the
<code>realm-management</code> client, roles from the master realm administration clients (such as <code><realm-name>-realm</code>),
and administrative realm roles on the master realm (such as <code>admin</code> or <code>create-realm</code>). Roles may be assigned
directly to the user, inherited through group membership, or obtained through composite roles.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The following restrictions apply to administrative users accessed through the SCIM API:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Read operations</strong> (<code>GET</code>) return a minimal representation containing only the <code>id</code>, <code>schemas</code>, and <code>userName</code>
attributes. Personal details such as <code>name</code> and <code>emails</code> are not included.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Write operations</strong> (<code>PUT</code>, <code>PATCH</code>, <code>DELETE</code>) return a <code>403 Forbidden</code> response.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Administrative users still appear in listing and search results, but always with the minimal representation.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Once all administrative roles are revoked from a user, the user becomes fully manageable through SCIM again.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="protected-admin-groups"><a class="anchor" href="#protected-admin-groups"></a>Protected admin groups</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A group is considered an administrative group if it holds any administrative role. This includes roles from the
<code>realm-management</code> client, roles from the master realm administration clients (such as <code><realm-name>-realm</code>),
and administrative realm roles on the master realm. Roles may be assigned directly to the group or obtained
through composite roles. Child groups of an administrative group are also protected, because their members
inherit the parent group’s administrative roles.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The following restrictions apply to administrative groups accessed through the SCIM API:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Read operations</strong> (<code>GET</code>) return a minimal representation containing only the <code>id</code>, <code>schemas</code>, and <code>displayName</code>
attributes. Members and other attributes are not included.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Write operations</strong> (<code>PUT</code>, <code>PATCH</code>, <code>DELETE</code>) return a <code>403 Forbidden</code> response.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Membership changes are blocked from both directions:</strong></p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Adding or removing members through a <code>PATCH</code> on the group resource returns <code>403 Forbidden</code>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Adding or removing a user to or from an administrative group through a <code>PATCH</code> on the user resource also
returns <code>403 Forbidden</code>.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Deletion is blocked for parent groups of an administrative group.</strong> Deleting a group whose subtree contains an
administrative group at any depth returns <code>403 Forbidden</code>, even if the parent group itself is not administrative,
to prevent an administrative group from being removed through a cascading delete.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Administrative groups still appear in listing and search results, but always with the minimal representation.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_understanding_scim_endpoints_"><a class="anchor" href="#_understanding_scim_endpoints_"></a>Understanding the SCIM endpoints</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/scim/understanding-scim-endpoints.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/scim/understanding-scim-endpoints.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/scim/understanding-scim-endpoints.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph _abstract">
<p>All SCIM endpoints use the <code>application/scim+json</code> content type for both requests and responses, as specified by RFC 7644.
The <code>application/json</code> content type is also accepted for requests.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="available-endpoints"><a class="anchor" href="#available-endpoints"></a>Available endpoints</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The following table summarizes all available and supported SCIM endpoints.</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33.3333%;">
<col style="width: 16.6666%;">
<col style="width: 50.0001%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Endpoint</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Methods</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>/Users</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">GET, POST</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">List all users or create a new user.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>/Users/{id}</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Retrieve, replace, partially update, or delete a specific user.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>/Users/.search</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">POST</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Search users using a request body (useful for complex or long filter expressions).</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>/Groups</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">GET, POST</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">List all groups or create a new group.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>/Groups/{id}</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Retrieve, replace, partially update, or delete a specific group.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>/Groups/.search</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">POST</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Search groups using a request body.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>/ServiceProviderConfig</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">GET</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Retrieve the SCIM capabilities supported by the server.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>/ResourceTypes</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">GET</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">List the resource types (User, Group) available on the server.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>/Schemas</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">GET</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">List all SCIM schemas supported by the server, including extensions.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>/Schemas/{id}</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">GET</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Retrieve a specific schema by its ID (URN).</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="http-methods"><a class="anchor" href="#http-methods"></a>HTTP methods</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The SCIM API supports the following HTTP methods for resource management:</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 25%;">
<col style="width: 25%;">
<col style="width: 50%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Method</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Status Code</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">POST</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">201 Created</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Create a new resource.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">GET</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">200 OK</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Retrieve a single resource by ID, or list/search resources.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">PUT</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">200 OK</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Replace an existing resource entirely.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">PATCH</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">200 OK</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Partially modify a resource using add, replace, or remove operations.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">DELETE</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">204 No Content</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Delete a resource.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="query-parameters"><a class="anchor" href="#query-parameters"></a>Query parameters</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The following query parameters can be used with GET requests to control the response. The same parameters
are also accepted in the body of <code>POST /.search</code> requests.</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 20%;">
<col style="width: 20%;">
<col style="width: 60%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Parameter</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Type</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>filter</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">String</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">A SCIM filter expression to search for resources. See <a href="#_scim_filtering_resources">Filtering resources</a>.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>startIndex</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Integer</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The 1-based index of the first result to return. Defaults to 1.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>count</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Integer</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The maximum number of results to return per page.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>attributes</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">String</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">A comma-separated list of attribute names to include in the response. When specified, only the listed attributes (plus <code>id</code> and <code>schemas</code>, which are always returned) are included.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>excludedAttributes</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">String</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">A comma-separated list of attribute names to exclude from the response. Applied after the <code>attributes</code> filter. The <code>id</code> attribute cannot be excluded.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>sortBy</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">String</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The attribute name to sort results by. See note below.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>sortOrder</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">String</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The sort order: <code>ascending</code> (default) or <code>descending</code>. See note below.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
While the <code>sortBy</code> and <code>sortOrder</code> parameters are accepted by the API, custom sorting is not currently
supported. Resources are returned in the default order used by the underlying store, consistent with the
behavior of the Keycloak Admin REST API.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="resource-metadata"><a class="anchor" href="#resource-metadata"></a>Resource metadata</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Every SCIM resource returned by the API includes a <code>meta</code> object with the following attributes:</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 25%;">
<col style="width: 75%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Attribute</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>resourceType</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The type of the resource (for example, <code>User</code> or <code>Group</code>).</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>created</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The timestamp when the resource was created, in ISO 8601 format.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>lastModified</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The timestamp when the resource was last modified, in ISO 8601 format.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>location</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The full URI of the resource (for example, <code>http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users/{id}</code>).</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_accessing_scim_service_provider_config_"><a class="anchor" href="#_accessing_scim_service_provider_config_"></a>Accessing the SCIM service provider configuration</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/scim/accessing-service-config.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/scim/accessing-service-config.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/scim/accessing-service-config.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>As per the SCIM specification, the Service Provider Configuration endpoint (<code>/ServiceProviderConfig</code>) provides metadata
about the capabilities available from the SCIM API.</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/ServiceProviderConfig \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/scim+json"</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A successful response returns the capabilities of the SCIM API, including supported operations such as
<code>patch</code>, <code>filter</code>, and the authentication schemes:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="json">{
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">schemas</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: [<span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:ServiceProviderConfig</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>],
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">patch</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: {
    <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">supported</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="value">true</span>
  },
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">bulk</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: {
    <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">supported</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="value">false</span>,
