    <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">maxOperations</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="integer">0</span>,
    <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">maxPayloadSize</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="integer">0</span>
  },
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">filter</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: {
    <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">supported</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="value">true</span>,
    <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">maxResults</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="integer">100</span>
  },
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">changePassword</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: {
    <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">supported</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="value">false</span>
  },
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">sort</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: {
    <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">supported</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="value">false</span>
  },
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">etag</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: {
    <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">supported</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="value">false</span>
  },
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">authenticationSchemes</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: [
    {
      <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">type</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">oauthbearertoken</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>,
      <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">name</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">OAuth Bearer Token</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>,
      <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">description</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">Authentication scheme using the OAuth Bearer Token standard</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>
    }
  ]
}</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>At the moment, the Service Provider Configuration is read-only and cannot be modified.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="supported-and-unsupported-capabilities"><a class="anchor" href="#supported-and-unsupported-capabilities"></a>Supported and unsupported capabilities</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The Service Provider Configuration reflects the capabilities implemented by Keycloak. The following optional
capabilities defined by RFC 7644 are <strong>not</strong> supported in this release:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Bulk operations</strong> (<code>bulk.supported</code> is <code>false</code>). There is no <code>/Bulk</code> endpoint; send one request per resource.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Sorting</strong> (<code>sort.supported</code> is <code>false</code>). The <code>sortBy</code> and <code>sortOrder</code> parameters are accepted but ignored, and resources
are returned in the default order of the underlying store.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>ETag / resource versioning</strong> (<code>etag.supported</code> is <code>false</code>). Resources do not carry a <code>meta.version</code>, and conditional
requests such as <code>If-Match</code> are not honored.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Password changes</strong> (<code>changePassword.supported</code> is <code>false</code>). The <code>password</code> attribute cannot be set or updated through
SCIM. Manage credentials through the Admin Console or the Admin REST API instead.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The <code>patch</code> and <code>filter</code> capabilities are supported. List and search requests return at most <code>100</code> results per request
(<code>filter.maxResults</code>); use pagination to retrieve additional results. See <a href="#_scim_filtering_resources">Filtering resources</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Future releases may allow customization of certain capabilities, such as supported authentication schemes or maximum filter results.
For now, the configuration reflects the default capabilities of the SCIM API as implemented in Keycloak.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_scim_managing_users_"><a class="anchor" href="#_scim_managing_users_"></a>Managing users</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/scim/managing-users.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/scim/managing-users.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/scim/managing-users.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph _abstract">
<p>The SCIM <code>/Users</code> endpoint allows you to create, read, update, and delete realm user resources in Keycloak. User resources
conform to the <code>urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User</code> schema as defined in RFC 7643.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="core-user-attributes"><a class="anchor" href="#core-user-attributes"></a>Core user attributes</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The following table shows the core SCIM user attributes and how they map to Keycloak user attributes:</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 25%;">
<col style="width: 25%;">
<col style="width: 50%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">SCIM Attribute</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Keycloak Attribute</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>userName</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>username</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Unique identifier for the user. Required.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>name.givenName</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>firstName</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Given name (first name).</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>name.familyName</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>lastName</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Family name (last name).</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>emails</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>email</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">User email addresses. Even though the attribute is multi-valued, Keycloak does not support mutiple emails for a
given user account. When multiple email values are submitted, only the first value is persisted. In SCIM responses, the stored address is returned as a single <code>work</code> email entry that is marked as <code>primary</code>.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>active</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>enabled</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Whether the user account is enabled.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>locale</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>locale</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">User locale. Only available when internationalization is enabled on the realm.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>externalId</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">(custom attribute)</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">An identifier from an external system. Requires user profile configuration. See <a href="#_scim_mapping_attributes_">Mapping attributes</a>.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Additional name sub-attributes (<code>name.middleName</code>, <code>name.honorificPrefix</code>, <code>name.honorificSuffix</code>) can be mapped
by configuring user profile attributes. See <a href="#_scim_mapping_attributes_">Mapping attributes</a> for details.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="creating-a-user"><a class="anchor" href="#creating-a-user"></a>Creating a user</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To create a user, send a <code>POST</code> request to the <code>/Users</code> endpoint. At minimum, you must provide a <code>userName</code>:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/scim+json" \
  -d '{
    "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],
    "userName": "jdoe",
    "name": {
      "givenName": "John",
      "familyName": "Doe"
    },
    "emails": [
      {
        "value": "jdoe@example.com",
        "type": "work",
        "primary": true
      }
    ],
    "active": true
  }'</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A successful response returns the created user with a <code>201 Created</code> status:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="json">{
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">schemas</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: [<span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>],
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">id</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>,
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">userName</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">jdoe</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>,
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">name</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: {
    <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">givenName</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">John</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>,
    <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">familyName</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">Doe</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>,
    <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">formatted</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">John Doe</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>
  },
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">emails</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: [
    {
      <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">value</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">jdoe@example.com</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>,
      <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">type</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">work</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>,
      <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">primary</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="value">true</span>
    }
  ],
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">active</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="value">true</span>,
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">meta</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: {
    <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">resourceType</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">User</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>,
    <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">created</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">2025-01-15T10:30:00Z</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>,
    <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">lastModified</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">2025-01-15T10:30:00Z</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>,
    <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">location</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>
  }
}</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
User profile validation rules are enforced when creating users through the SCIM API. If a required attribute
is missing or a value does not match the expected format, the API returns a <code>400 Bad Request</code> response with a
description of the validation error.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If a user with the same <code>userName</code> already exists, the API returns a <code>409 Conflict</code> response with
<code>scimType: "uniqueness"</code>.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
User creation through SCIM follows the same rules as user creation through the Admin REST API. If the realm
has a user storage provider (for example, LDAP) configured to synchronize registrations, the new user may be created
in that external provider instead of in the local Keycloak database. If the provider does not import users
into the local database, the created user is not retrievable through subsequent SCIM <code>GET</code>, list, search, or
<code>DELETE</code> requests, even though the <code>POST</code> request itself succeeds. This is a known limitation of the current
version of the SCIM API - see the notes on federated users under "Listing users" and "Deleting a user" below.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="retrieving-a-user"><a class="anchor" href="#retrieving-a-user"></a>Retrieving a user</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To retrieve a user by ID:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users/{id} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/scim+json"</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="listing-users"><a class="anchor" href="#listing-users"></a>Listing users</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To list all users in the realm:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/scim+json"</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The response uses the SCIM list format:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="json">{
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">schemas</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: [<span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:ListResponse</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>],
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">totalResults</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="integer">2</span>,
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">itemsPerPage</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="integer">2</span>,
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">startIndex</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="integer">1</span>,
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">Resources</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: [<span class="error">.</span><span class="error">.</span><span class="error">.</span>]
}</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For filtering and pagination of results, see <a href="#_scim_filtering_resources">Filtering resources</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
The SCIM <code>/Users</code> endpoint only returns users that are stored locally in the Keycloak database. Users
that are managed by external user federation providers (such as LDAP or custom providers) and have not been imported
into Keycloak are not included in SCIM search results. Federated users that have been imported (that is,
synchronized into the local database) are included. This is because Keycloak acts as the identity authority
only for locally stored users - external identity sources should expose their own SCIM endpoints for managing
their users.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="selecting-attributes"><a class="anchor" href="#selecting-attributes"></a>Selecting attributes</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can control which attributes are included in the response for both single-resource and list requests
by using the <code>attributes</code> query parameter:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl "http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users/{id}?attributes=userName,emails" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/scim+json"</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Or exclude certain attributes from the response:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl "http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users/{id}?excludedAttributes=name" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/scim+json"</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When requesting a parent attribute (for example, <code>name</code>), all its sub-attributes are returned. When requesting
a sub-attribute (for example, <code>name.familyName</code>), only that specific sub-attribute is included.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
Attribute names in query parameters are case-insensitive, as specified by RFC 7644. The <code>id</code> and <code>schemas</code>
attributes are always included and cannot be excluded.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="updating-a-user"><a class="anchor" href="#updating-a-user"></a>Updating a user</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To fully replace a user resource, send a <code>PUT</code> request:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl -X PUT http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users/{id} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/scim+json" \
  -d '{
    "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],
    "id": "{id}",
    "userName": "jdoe",
    "name": {
      "givenName": "John",
      "familyName": "Smith"
    },
    "emails": [
      {
        "value": "john.smith@example.com",
        "type": "work",
        "primary": true
      }
    ],
    "active": true
  }'</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The <code>id</code> in the request body must match the <code>id</code> in the URL path, otherwise the API returns a <code>400 Bad Request</code> error.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="partially-updating-a-user"><a class="anchor" href="#partially-updating-a-user"></a>Partially updating a user</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The <code>PATCH</code> method allows you to modify specific attributes without replacing the entire resource. A patch request
contains one or more operations, each specifying an action (<code>add</code>, <code>replace</code>, or <code>remove</code>), an optional path to
the attribute, and a value.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
A single PATCH request can contain at most 100 operations. Requests exceeding this limit are rejected with
a <code>400 Bad Request</code> response and <code>scimType: "tooMany"</code>.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="adding-or-replacing-attributes"><a class="anchor" href="#adding-or-replacing-attributes"></a>Adding or replacing attributes</h5>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users/{id} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/scim+json" \
  -d '{
    "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
    "Operations": [
      {
        "op": "replace",
        "path": "name.givenName",
        "value": "Jane"
      },
      {
        "op": "replace",
        "path": "active",
        "value": false
      },
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "emails",
        "value": {
          "value": "jane@example.com",
          "type": "work",
          "primary": true
        }
      }
    ]
  }'</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can also provide multiple attributes in a single operation without specifying a path. In this case, the paths
are derived from the JSON structure:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users/{id} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/scim+json" \
  -d '{
    "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
    "Operations": [
      {
        "op": "replace",
        "value": {
          "name": {"givenName": "Jane"},
          "active": false
        }
      }
    ]
  }'</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="removing-attributes"><a class="anchor" href="#removing-attributes"></a>Removing attributes</h5>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users/{id} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/scim+json" \
  -d '{
    "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
    "Operations": [
      {
        "op": "remove",
        "path": "name.honorificPrefix"
      }
    ]
  }'</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For multi-valued attributes, you can use a filter in the path to remove specific values.
For complex multivalued attributes like <code>groups</code>, only filtering by the <code>value</code> sub-attribute is supported.
See the "Filtering limitations in PATCH operations" section below for details.</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users/{id} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/scim+json" \
  -d '{
    "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
    "Operations": [
      {
        "op": "remove",
        "path": "groups[value eq \"<group-id>\"]"
      }
    ]
  }'</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="filtering-limitations-in-patch-operations"><a class="anchor" href="#filtering-limitations-in-patch-operations"></a>Filtering limitations in PATCH operations</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Filtering in PATCH remove operations is supported only for multivalued attributes (both complex attributes like <code>groups</code> and custom scalar multivalued extension attributes).
For complex multivalued attributes like <code>groups</code>, only the <code>value</code> sub-attribute (the unique identifier) is supported for filtering. You can use the <code>eq</code> (equal) comparison operator optionally combined with the <code>or</code> logical operator.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For scalar multivalued attributes (extension attributes without a complex type), only the <code>eq</code> operator is supported, optionally combined with the <code>or</code> logical operator.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
The <code>and</code> operator is not supported for any multivalued attributes because a single value cannot satisfy two conditions simultaneously. For example, <code>affiliation[value eq "member" and value eq "faculty"]</code> is logically impossible since one scalar value cannot equal both "member" AND "faculty" at the same time. For complex attributes, filtering is restricted to the <code>value</code> sub-attribute, making AND equally invalid. Use <code>or</code> to match multiple values instead: <code>affiliation[value eq "member" or value eq "faculty"]</code>.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>All other comparison operators are not supported.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="managing-group-membership"><a class="anchor" href="#managing-group-membership"></a>Managing group membership</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can manage a user’s group memberships directly through the user resource. Group membership can also be managed
from the group side using the <code>/Groups</code> endpoint. See <a href="#_scim_managing_groups_">Managing groups</a> for details.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="adding-a-user-to-groups-on-creation"><a class="anchor" href="#adding-a-user-to-groups-on-creation"></a>Adding a user to groups on creation</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When creating a user, you can specify the groups the user should belong to:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/scim+json" \
  -d '{
    "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],
    "userName": "jdoe",
    "groups": [
      {"value": "{groupId}"}
    ]
  }'</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="modifying-group-membership-via-patch"><a class="anchor" href="#modifying-group-membership-via-patch"></a>Modifying group membership via PATCH</h5>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users/{id} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/scim+json" \
  -d '{
    "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
    "Operations": [
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "groups",
        "value": "{groupId}"
      }
    ]
  }'</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To remove a user from a group:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users/{id} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/scim+json" \
  -d '{
    "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
    "Operations": [
      {
        "op": "remove",
        "path": "groups[value eq \"{groupId}\"]"
      }
    ]
  }'</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="querying-group-membership"><a class="anchor" href="#querying-group-membership"></a>Querying group membership</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To retrieve a user’s groups, include <code>groups</code> in the <code>attributes</code> parameter:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl "http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users/{id}?attributes=groups" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/scim+json"</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Each group membership includes the group <code>value</code> (ID), <code>display</code> (name), and <code>type</code> (<code>direct</code> or <code>indirect</code> for
inherited memberships from parent groups).</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="deleting-a-user"><a class="anchor" href="#deleting-a-user"></a>Deleting a user</h4>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users/{id} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN"</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A successful deletion returns a <code>204 No Content</code> response with no body.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
Like other SCIM operations, <code>DELETE</code> only operates on users that can be resolved from local storage. Deleting
a user that was created in a federation provider but was never imported into the local Keycloak database
returns a <code>404 Not Found</code> response, even if creation of that user through SCIM previously succeeded.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_scim_managing_groups_"><a class="anchor" href="#_scim_managing_groups_"></a>Managing groups</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/scim/managing-groups.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/scim/managing-groups.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/scim/managing-groups.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph _abstract">
<p>The SCIM <code>/Groups</code> endpoint allows you to create, read, update, and delete realm group resources in Keycloak. Group resources
conform to the <code>urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group</code> schema as defined in RFC 7643.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="group-attributes"><a class="anchor" href="#group-attributes"></a>Group attributes</h4>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 25%;">
<col style="width: 25%;">
<col style="width: 50%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">SCIM Attribute</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Keycloak Attribute</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>displayName</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>name</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The name of the group. Required.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>externalId</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">(custom attribute)</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">An identifier from an external system.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>members</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">(group membership)</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">List of users that belong to this group. Read-only on GET; managed via PATCH.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="creating-a-group"><a class="anchor" href="#creating-a-group"></a>Creating a group</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To create a group, send a <code>POST</code> request to the <code>/Groups</code> endpoint:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Groups \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/scim+json" \
  -d '{
    "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group"],
    "displayName": "Engineering Team",
    "externalId": "eng-team-001"
  }'</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A successful response returns the created group with a <code>201 Created</code> status.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
Group members cannot be specified during group creation. Attempting to include members in the <code>POST</code>
request results in a <code>400 Bad Request</code> error. Use the <code>PATCH</code> method to add members after creating the group.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If a group with the same <code>displayName</code> already exists, the API returns a <code>409 Conflict</code> response with
<code>scimType: "uniqueness"</code>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="retrieving-a-group"><a class="anchor" href="#retrieving-a-group"></a>Retrieving a group</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To retrieve a group by ID:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Groups/{id} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/scim+json"</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="listing-groups"><a class="anchor" href="#listing-groups"></a>Listing groups</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To list all groups in the realm:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Groups \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/scim+json"</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For filtering and pagination of results, see <a href="#_scim_filtering_resources">Filtering resources</a>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="updating-a-group"><a class="anchor" href="#updating-a-group"></a>Updating a group</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To replace a group’s attributes, send a <code>PUT</code> request:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl -X PUT http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Groups/{id} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/scim+json" \
  -d '{
    "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group"],
    "id": "{id}",
    "displayName": "Platform Engineering",
    "externalId": "eng-team-002"
  }'</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
Group members cannot be modified through <code>PUT</code> requests. Attempting to include members in the <code>PUT</code>
request results in a <code>400 Bad Request</code> error. Use the <code>PATCH</code> method to manage group members.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="partially-updating-a-group"><a class="anchor" href="#partially-updating-a-group"></a>Partially updating a group</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To modify specific group attributes, use a <code>PATCH</code> request.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
A single PATCH request can contain at most 100 operations. Requests exceeding this limit are rejected with
a <code>400 Bad Request</code> response and <code>scimType: "tooMany"</code>.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Groups/{id} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/scim+json" \
  -d '{
    "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
    "Operations": [
      {
        "op": "replace",
        "path": "displayName",
        "value": "Platform Engineering"
      }
    ]
  }'</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="managing-group-members"><a class="anchor" href="#managing-group-members"></a>Managing group members</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Group membership is managed exclusively through <code>PATCH</code> operations on the group resource. Group membership can also
be managed from the user side through the <code>/Users</code> endpoint. See <a href="#_scim_managing_users_">Managing users</a> for details.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="adding-members"><a class="anchor" href="#adding-members"></a>Adding members</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To add users to a group:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Groups/{groupId} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/scim+json" \
  -d '{
    "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
    "Operations": [
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "members",
        "value": "{userId1}"
      },
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "members",
        "value": "{userId2}"
      }
    ]
  }'</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="removing-members"><a class="anchor" href="#removing-members"></a>Removing members</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To remove specific members from a group, use a value path filter:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Groups/{groupId} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/scim+json" \
  -d '{
    "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
    "Operations": [
      {
        "op": "remove",
        "path": "members[value eq \"{userId}\"]"
      }
    ]
  }'</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can remove multiple members in a single operation using the <code>or</code> operator:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Groups/{groupId} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/scim+json" \
  -d '{
    "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
    "Operations": [
      {
        "op": "remove",
        "path": "members[value eq \"{userId1}\" or value eq \"{userId2}\"]"
      }
    ]
  }'</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="filtering-limitations-in-patch-operations-2"><a class="anchor" href="#filtering-limitations-in-patch-operations-2"></a>Filtering limitations in PATCH operations</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Filtering in PATCH remove operations is supported only for multivalued attributes (such as <code>members</code>).
For complex multivalued attributes like <code>members</code>, only the <code>value</code> sub-attribute (the unique identifier) is supported for filtering. You can use the <code>eq</code> (equal) comparison operator optionally combined with the <code>or</code> logical operator.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
The <code>and</code> operator is not supported for any multivalued attributes because a single value cannot satisfy two conditions simultaneously. For example, <code>members[value eq "user1-id" and value eq "user2-id"]</code> is logically impossible since one member ID cannot equal two different IDs at the same time. Use <code>or</code> to match multiple values instead: <code>members[value eq "user1-id" or value eq "user2-id"]</code>.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>All other comparison operators and sub-attributes are not supported.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="querying-members"><a class="anchor" href="#querying-members"></a>Querying members</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To retrieve a group’s members, include <code>members</code> in the <code>attributes</code> parameter:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl "http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Groups/{groupId}?attributes=members" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/scim+json"</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Each member entry includes:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>value</code>: The user ID.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>display</code>: The user’s username.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>type</code>: Always <code>User</code>.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="bidirectional-membership"><a class="anchor" href="#bidirectional-membership"></a>Bidirectional membership</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Group membership is bidirectional. When a user is added to a group, the user’s <code>groups</code> attribute also reflects
the membership. Similarly, when a user is assigned to a group through the User resource, the group’s <code>members</code>
list is updated accordingly.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can also find groups by member:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl "http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Groups?filter=members.value+eq+\"{userId}\"" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/scim+json"</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
Organization-related groups cannot have their members managed through the SCIM API. Attempting to add or
remove members from an organization group returns a <code>400 Bad Request</code> error. Use the Organization API to manage
organization group memberships.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="deleting-a-group"><a class="anchor" href="#deleting-a-group"></a>Deleting a group</h4>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Groups/{id} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN"</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A successful deletion returns a <code>204 No Content</code> response.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_scim_filtering_resources"><a class="anchor" href="#_scim_filtering_resources"></a>Filtering resources</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/scim/filtering-resources.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/scim/filtering-resources.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/scim/filtering-resources.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph _abstract">
<p>The SCIM API in Keycloak supports the full filter syntax defined in <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7644#section-3.4.2.2">RFC 7644, Section 3.4.2.2</a>,
allowing you to search for resources using a rich expression language.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="using-filters"><a class="anchor" href="#using-filters"></a>Using filters</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Filters are specified using the <code>filter</code> query parameter on <code>GET</code> requests:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl "http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users?filter=userName+eq+\"jdoe\"" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/scim+json"</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
Filter values must be URL-encoded when used in query parameters. Spaces in the filter expression should be
encoded as <code>+</code> or <code>%20</code>. The examples in this section show the raw filter syntax for readability.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="comparison-operators"><a class="anchor" href="#comparison-operators"></a>Comparison operators</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The following comparison operators are supported:</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 16.6666%;">
<col style="width: 33.3333%;">
<col style="width: 50.0001%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Operator</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Example</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>eq</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Equal</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>userName eq "jdoe"</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>ne</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Not equal</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>active ne false</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>co</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Contains</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>emails co "example.com"</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>sw</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Starts with</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>userName sw "j"</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>ew</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Ends with</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>userName ew "doe"</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>gt</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Greater than</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>meta.created gt "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>ge</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Greater than or equal</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>meta.created ge "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>lt</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Less than</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>meta.lastModified lt "2025-06-01T00:00:00Z"</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>le</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Less than or equal</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>meta.lastModified le "2025-06-01T00:00:00Z"</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>pr</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Present (attribute has a value)</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>emails.value pr</code></p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
The <code>gt</code>, <code>ge</code>, <code>lt</code>, and <code>le</code> operators are supported on date/time attributes such as <code>meta.created</code> and
<code>meta.lastModified</code>. The <code>sw</code>, <code>ew</code>, and <code>co</code> operators are supported on string attributes but not on date/time
or boolean attributes. Invalid operator/type combinations return a <code>400 Bad Request</code> response with
<code>scimType: "invalidFilter"</code>.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_scim_filtering_null_values"><a class="anchor" href="#_scim_filtering_null_values"></a>Attributes without a value</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A comparison such as <code>attribute eq "value"</code> or <code>attribute ne "value"</code> does not match resources where the attribute
has no value. Use <code>not (attribute pr)</code> to find them. For a multi-valued attribute, <code>attribute ne "value"</code> matches
resources that have at least one other value.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The <code>eq</code> and <code>ne</code> operators accept the <code>null</code> literal, but the comparison never matches, so it cannot be used to find
resources without a value.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="logical-operators"><a class="anchor" href="#logical-operators"></a>Logical operators</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Filters can be combined using logical operators:</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 25%;">
<col style="width: 75%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Operator</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>and</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Both conditions must be true.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>or</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">At least one condition must be true.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>not</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Negates the following expression. Parentheses are optional but recommended for clarity.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="examples"><a class="anchor" href="#examples"></a>Examples</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Filter users by family name and active status:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre>name.familyName eq "Smith" and active eq true</pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Filter users matching either condition:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre>userName eq "jdoe" or userName eq "asmith"</pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Negate a condition:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre>not (active eq false)</pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Use parentheses to group conditions:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre>(userName sw "j" or userName sw "a") and active eq true</pre>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="filtering-by-sub-attributes"><a class="anchor" href="#filtering-by-sub-attributes"></a>Filtering by sub-attributes</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can filter by sub-attributes of complex attributes using dot notation:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre>name.givenName eq "John"
name.familyName sw "Sm"</pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For multi-valued attributes like <code>emails</code>:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre>emails eq "jdoe@example.com"
emails.value eq "jdoe@example.com"
emails co "example.com"</pre>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="value-path-filters"><a class="anchor" href="#value-path-filters"></a>Value path filters</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>SCIM also supports value path filtering, where you filter on sub-attributes within a complex attribute using
bracket notation:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre>name[familyName eq "Smith"]
name[givenName eq "John" and familyName eq "Doe"]
name[givenName eq "John" or givenName eq "Jane"]</pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Value path filters can be combined with regular filters:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre>name[familyName eq "Smith"] and active eq true</pre>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="filtering-by-group-membership"><a class="anchor" href="#filtering-by-group-membership"></a>Filtering by group membership</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can filter users by their group membership using the <code>groups.value</code> attribute:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl "http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users?filter=groups.value+eq+\"{groupId}\"" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/scim+json"</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Combine group membership filters with logical operators:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre>(groups.value eq "{groupIdA}") and (groups.value eq "{groupIdB}")
(groups.value eq "{groupIdA}") or (groups.value eq "{groupIdB}")</pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Similarly, you can filter groups by member:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl "http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Groups?filter=members.value+eq+\"{userId}\"" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/scim+json"</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
When fine-grained admin permissions (FGAP) are enabled, only the <code>eq</code> operator is supported for
<code>groups.value</code> and <code>members.value</code> filter paths. The server verifies that the caller has <code>view</code> permission
on the specific group or user being matched. Other operators (<code>ne</code>, <code>pr</code>, <code>co</code>, <code>sw</code>, <code>gt</code>, etc.) cannot be
safely authorized because they can match rows the caller is not permitted to see, so they silently return
empty results for these paths. For the same reason, negating an equality condition on these paths (for example,
<code>not (groups.value eq "{groupId}")</code>) also returns empty results, because it is equivalent to the unsupported
<code>ne</code> operator. This restriction does not apply to any other filter attributes, and does not apply when FGAP is
disabled, where the full set of operators is available on these paths.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
When an LDAP user federation provider is configured with a group mapper in <code>LDAP_ONLY</code> mode, group
membership filters (<code>groups.value</code> and <code>members.value</code>) may return empty results. This happens because
<code>LDAP_ONLY</code> mode stores group memberships exclusively in LDAP, while the SCIM filter queries the local
database directly. Retrieving a user’s groups via <code>?attributes=groups</code> or a group’s members via
<code>?attributes=members</code> is not affected, as those requests go through the federation layer and read from LDAP.
If you need membership-based filtering with LDAP federation, consider switching the group mapper to <code>IMPORT</code>
mode so that memberships are also stored locally.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="filtering-by-extension-attributes"><a class="anchor" href="#filtering-by-extension-attributes"></a>Filtering by extension attributes</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Filters can reference attributes from schema extensions by using the full schema URI as a prefix:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre>urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User:department eq "Engineering"
urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User:manager.displayName ew "Manager"</pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For custom schema extensions:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre>urn:my:params:scim:schemas:extension:custom:1.0:User:myattribute eq "myvalue"</pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>See <a href="#_scim_managing_schema_extensions_">Managing schema extensions</a> for more details on configuring extension attributes.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="using-post-based-search"><a class="anchor" href="#using-post-based-search"></a>Using POST-based search</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For complex queries that might exceed URL length limitations, use the <code>POST /.search</code> endpoint:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users/.search \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/scim+json" \
  -d '{
    "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:SearchRequest"],
    "filter": "(userName sw \"j\" or userName sw \"a\") and active eq true",
    "startIndex": 1,
    "count": 10,
    "attributes": ["userName", "emails"]
  }'</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The search request body supports the same parameters available as query parameters: <code>filter</code>, <code>startIndex</code>,
<code>count</code>, <code>attributes</code>, <code>excludedAttributes</code>, <code>sortBy</code>, and <code>sortOrder</code>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="pagination"><a class="anchor" href="#pagination"></a>Pagination</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When listing or searching resources, you can control the page of results returned using the <code>startIndex</code> and
<code>count</code> parameters:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl "http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users?startIndex=1&count=10" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/scim+json"</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The response includes pagination metadata:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="json">{
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">schemas</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: [<span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:ListResponse</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>],
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">totalResults</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="integer">45</span>,
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">itemsPerPage</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="integer">10</span>,
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">startIndex</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="integer">1</span>,
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">Resources</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: [<span class="error">.</span><span class="error">.</span><span class="error">.</span>]
}</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>totalResults</code>: The total number of resources matching the query.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>itemsPerPage</code>: The number of resources in the current page.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>startIndex</code>: The 1-based index of the first resource in the current page.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To retrieve the next page, increment <code>startIndex</code> by <code>count</code>:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">curl "http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/scim/v2/Users?startIndex=11&count=10" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/scim+json"</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="filtering-constraints-and-limitations"><a class="anchor" href="#filtering-constraints-and-limitations"></a>Filtering constraints and limitations</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Keep the following constraints in mind when building filter expressions. These are intended behaviors and should not be
reported as defects.</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Result size is capped.</strong> A list or search request returns at most 100 results. If <code>count</code> is omitted or greater
than 100, it is treated as 100 (<code>filter.maxResults</code>). Use pagination (see <a href="#pagination">Pagination</a>) to retrieve additional results.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Filter length is limited.</strong> A filter expression may not exceed 2048 characters. Longer expressions are rejected with a
<code>400 Bad Request</code> and <code>scimType: "invalidFilter"</code>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Nesting depth is limited.</strong> The combined nesting of grouping parentheses and value path brackets may not exceed 10
levels. Deeper expressions are rejected with a <code>400 Bad Request</code> and <code>scimType: "invalidFilter"</code>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Sorting is not applied.</strong> The <code>sortBy</code> and <code>sortOrder</code> parameters are accepted but ignored. Results are returned in the
default order of the underlying store, consistent with the Keycloak Admin REST API.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>The <code>and</code> operator cannot be used to match multiple values within the same multivalued array.</strong> For example,
<code>groups[value eq "{groupIdA}" and value eq "{groupIdB}"]</code> is rejected because a single group element cannot have two values
simultaneously. Use <code>or</code> to match either value.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Operator and attribute-type compatibility is enforced.</strong> String operators (<code>sw</code>, <code>ew</code>, <code>co</code>) cannot be used on
date/time or boolean attributes, and incompatible combinations are rejected. See <a href="#comparison-operators">Comparison operators</a>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Comparisons skip attributes without a value.</strong> <code>attribute ne "value"</code> and <code>attribute eq null</code> do not match resources
where the attribute has no value. Use <code>not (attribute pr)</code> to find them. See <a href="#_scim_filtering_null_values">Attributes without a value</a>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Membership filters carry extra restrictions.</strong> The <code>groups.value</code> and <code>members.value</code> paths behave differently under
fine-grained admin permissions and with LDAP <code>LDAP_ONLY</code> group mappers. See <a href="#filtering-by-group-membership">Filtering by group membership</a>.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="error-responses"><a class="anchor" href="#error-responses"></a>Error responses</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Invalid filter expressions return a <code>400 Bad Request</code> response with <code>scimType: "invalidFilter"</code>:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="json">{
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">schemas</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: [<span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:Error</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>],
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">scimType</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">invalidFilter</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>,
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">detail</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">Invalid filter expression</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>,
  <span class="key"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">status</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>: <span class="string"><span class="delimiter">"</span><span class="content">400</span><span class="delimiter">"</span></span>
}</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Common causes of filter errors:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Mismatched parentheses.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Unknown filter operators.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Using an operator on an incompatible attribute type (for example, <code>gt</code> on a boolean).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Using string operators (<code>sw</code>, <code>ew</code>, <code>co</code>) on date/time attributes.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Using <code>null</code> with an operator other than <code>eq</code> or <code>ne</code>.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_scim_mapping_attributes_"><a class="anchor" href="#_scim_mapping_attributes_"></a>Mapping user attributes to SCIM schemas</h3>
<div class="sidebarblock page-links">
<div class="content">
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/tree/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/scim/mapping-attributes.adoc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this section</a>
<a href="https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=Docs:%20server_admin/topics/scim/mapping-attributes.adoc&description=%0A%0AFile:%20server_admin/topics/scim/mapping-attributes.adoc&version=26.8.1&behaviorExpected=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20you%20want%20to%20see%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&behaviorActual=%3C!--%20describe%20what%20is%20currently%20wrong%20or%20missing%20in%20the%20docs%20--%3E&reproducer=%3C!--%20list%20steps%20in%20the%20application%20that%20show%20behavior%20that%20should%20be%20documented%20--%3E" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Report an issue</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph _abstract">
<p>Keycloak uses the User Profile configuration to define how user attributes are mapped to SCIM schema attributes.
A set of core attributes are mapped by default, and additional attributes can be mapped by configuring user profile
attributes with a SCIM schema attribute mapping.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="default-attribute-mappings"><a class="anchor" href="#default-attribute-mappings"></a>Default attribute mappings</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The following attributes are automatically mapped to the SCIM core user schema (<code>urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User</code>)
without any additional configuration:</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%;">
<col style="width: 50%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Keycloak Attribute</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">SCIM Attribute</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>username</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>userName</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>email</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>emails</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>firstName</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>name.givenName</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>lastName</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>name.familyName</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>enabled</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>active</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>createdTimestamp</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>meta.created</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>locale</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>locale</code> (only when internationalization is enabled)</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="supported-core-multivalued-and-complex-attributes"><a class="anchor" href="#supported-core-multivalued-and-complex-attributes"></a>Supported core multivalued and complex attributes</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7643#section-4.1.2">RFC 7643, Section 4.1.2</a> defines a set of multivalued
attributes for the core User schema (<code>urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User</code>). Keycloak supports a
subset of these attributes natively. The following table lists the core multivalued and complex attributes and
their support status:</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 25%;">
<col style="width: 25%;">
<col style="width: 50%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">SCIM Attribute</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Supported</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Notes</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>emails</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Yes</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Exposed as a multivalued attribute, but backed by the single Keycloak <code>email</code> attribute. Only the first
value is stored and returned. See <a href="#_scim_managing_users_">Managing users</a> for details.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>groups</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Yes</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Reflects the user’s group memberships. Group memberships can be set during user creation and managed through
PATCH operations on the user resource. See <a href="#_scim_managing_users_">Managing users</a> for details. Group membership
can also be managed from the group side using group PATCH operations. See <a href="#_scim_managing_groups_">Managing groups</a> for details.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>name</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Yes</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">A single complex attribute. Its sub-attributes are mapped from user profile attributes. See
<a href="#mapping-additional-name-attributes">Mapping additional name attributes</a>.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>phoneNumbers</code>, <code>ims</code>, <code>photos</code>, <code>entitlements</code>, <code>roles</code>, <code>x509Certificates</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">No</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Not defined in the Keycloak core User schema. You cannot map a user profile attribute to these attributes
under the core schema URN. To expose equivalent data, use a schema extension or a custom multivalued mapping
instead. See <a href="#mapping-multivalued-attributes">Mapping multivalued attributes</a> and <a href="#_scim_managing_schema_extensions_">Managing schema extensions</a>.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>addresses</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">No</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Not supported. This is a complex multivalued attribute whose mapping to user profile attributes requires
further work and is not available in this release.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="adding-custom-attribute-mappings"><a class="anchor" href="#adding-custom-attribute-mappings"></a>Adding custom attribute mappings</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To map additional user attributes to SCIM schema attributes, you need to create a user profile attribute and
configure its SCIM schema attribute mapping, setting the value to the SCIM attribute path that the user profile
attribute should be mapped to.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="using-the-admin-console-3"><a class="anchor" href="#using-the-admin-console-3"></a>Using the Admin Console</h5>
<div class="olist arabic">
<div class="title">Procedure</div>
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Realm settings</strong> in the menu, then select the <strong>User profile</strong> tab.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Create attribute</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Enter the <strong>Name</strong> for the attribute (for example, <code>middleName</code>).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>In the <strong>SCIM</strong> section, select or enter the <strong>SCIM attribute</strong> to map to (for example, <code>name.middleName</code>). Attributes
from the core User and Enterprise User schemas are available for selection. You can also enter custom values
for attributes from other schemas by typing the full URN-prefixed value (for example,
<code>urn:my:params:scim:schemas:extension:custom:1.0:User:memberOf</code>).
See <a href="#_scim_managing_schema_extensions_">Managing schema extensions</a> for more details on custom schemas.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Configure the attribute permissions as needed. At minimum, grant <strong>admin</strong> view access for the attribute
to appear in SCIM responses, and <strong>admin</strong> edit access for the attribute to be writable. See
<a href="#attribute-permissions-and-scim">Attribute permissions and SCIM</a> for details.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<div class="title">Configuring a SCIM attribute mapping in User Profile</div>
<p><span class="image"><img src="./images/scim-user-profile-mapping.png" alt="Configuring a SCIM attribute mapping"></span></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="attribute-permissions-and-scim"><a class="anchor" href="#attribute-permissions-and-scim"></a>Attribute permissions and SCIM</h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>SCIM operates as an admin-level API and uses the same User Profile permission model as the Admin API. The
permissions configured on a user profile attribute determine whether the attribute is visible and writable
through SCIM.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="visibility"><a class="anchor" href="#visibility"></a>Visibility</h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Custom attributes are only included in SCIM responses if they have admin <strong>view</strong> permissions. Attributes without
any view roles configured are not exposed through SCIM - they will not appear in GET responses, schema discovery,
or search results.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
